title: P1-A00 · Announcer copy: Australianisms slice and the Playtest-1 cue script
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-A00** (cites §15 A; master §10.10); master cut V2-112/V2-113 slice, R53, R55, R69 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D5` · **Track:** `audio` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** none; can start immediately.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Own the words the announcer says and the moment list A01 renders and A03 plays (nobody owned them: the audition sheet held placeholder lines,
and A01/A03 listed different moments). An R53 research slice scoped to Playtest-1 announcer lines plus the cue sheet as the one shared
moment vocabulary.

## Scope (owned paths)
`docs/copy/australianisms.md`, `tools/audio/cues-playtest1.tsv` (the cue sheet), the sheet loader check (used by A01's render).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Rendering (A01), playback/captions (A03). Award titles, car blurbs and the name generator stay V2-112 (Full).

## Contract and design decisions
(1) **Research pass (R53)**, scoped to what the announcer says in Playtest 1: Australian slang and references that fit announcer lines (master §10.10
examples are a start). Each term: meaning, where it fits, a family-friendly flag, a regional/cultural sensitivity note (no slurs, nothing
punching down, no Indigenous cultural terms used as jokes) and a source (e.g. the Australian National Dictionary Centre).
(2) **Cue script:** moment IDs are the one vocabulary A01 and A03 share. At least: welcome, countdown, final lap, door off, wheel off, big air,
late joiner, photo finish, winner, next round; plus any other moment the Playtest-1 loop can detect (e.g. wreck, lead change), each naming the
game event that fires it. Repeating moments get **≥ 4 variants** (a floor, not a cap) and a no-immediate-repeat rule for A03; once-a-round
moments get ≥ 2. Each row: moment ID, variant, trigger event, spoken text, caption text, delivery (`hype` or `warm`; A01 maps to a clone
reference), slang terms used, family-friendly flag.
DEFAULTs: every shipped line is family-friendly; lines work for any car: **no player names (R69)** and, in Playtest 1, **no car numbers or
colours** (a spliced number catalogue for any N stays Full, R55, Q-A5); in-race callouts ~8 words. **Guardrail in the tool:** the sheet loader
A01's render uses rejects a sheet that breaks these rules. Owner reviews when convenient; a rejected line becomes a repair bead (never blocks).

## Interfaces
- Provides: the cue sheet to A01 (render) and A03 (triggers + captions); the glossary to U01's copy voice.

## Required tests
- The loader check in the wave: passes on the real sheet; refuses a sheet with a missing caption, an unflagged line or a player name.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
The two files + the loader check's wave run (`on:any`). Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-A00/`.

## How this bead closes

## Working rules
Follow `AGENTS.md` (owner rules first) and `docs/process/bead-workflow.md`: check your own area, commit with `P1-A00` and the bead ID in the message, push, and close this bead once CI is green on a commit containing it (gate pass, ticked items, `receipt:<run url>`).

## Anti-narrowing clause
> Done only when the FELT, observable outcome above holds in the RUNNING game via the real host path. Passing unit/geometry tests is necessary but NOT sufficient.

- [x] [ev:ci] `docs/copy/australianisms.md` has the table, with every term sourced and flagged.
- [x] [ev:ci] `cues-playtest1.tsv` covers every moment A03 triggers, with the variant floors, captions, delivery and flags.
- [x] [ev:ci] The loader check passes in the wave and refuses a sheet with a missing caption, an unflagged line or a player name.

title: P1-A01 · Announcer voice (owner clone) and Playtest-1 cues
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-A01** (cites §15 A (incl. Audio on Apple hosts)); master cut V2-90/V2-113 slice, R89 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D5` · **Track:** `audio` · **Machine:** `on:eris` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-A00. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Status notes
**Already under way outside the tracker:** eris setup scripts, `voice_clone.py` and the audition cue sheet exist (commits 680afe8, d9de2d0);
start from them, not from scratch. The owner's reference recording is calm and the clone copies its delivery, so the first renders had "zero
excitement". `voice_energy.py` (commit 1ac11a2) builds an excited reference in the owner's timbre: VoiceDesign performs, Seed-VC converts with the
pitch contour kept, and the result becomes the clone reference. Its F0-mode candidate measured +6 to +9 semitones over the owner, speaker
similarity 0.96–0.97 and zero WER on four cues; the owner hasn't picked yet (E4f candidate). Re-recording a performed reference is the fallback.
Audio is generated on **eris** (`ssh eris`, workspace `~/Work/dev/jammers-audio`), never in this repo (R89); weights/recordings never committed.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Render every row of A00's cue sheet in the owner's cloned voice (Qwen3-TTS 1.7B on eris), screen the takes automatically, export the best as
self-hosted audio, and make regeneration one command. Owner approval is not a gate: candidates play in previews and the owner judges them at a
playtest; a rejected cue becomes a repair bead.

## Scope (owned paths)
`tools/audio/` (scripts; the cue sheet is A00's), `assets/audio/voice/`; private renders stay on eris. Also writes the `jammers-audio` skill from `tools/audio/README.md`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The copy (A00), runtime playback (A03), music (A02).

## Contract and design decisions
- Transcribe the owner's reference with **FrankenWhisper** (full Whisper large-v3).
- Build each Qwen3-TTS 1.7B Base clone prompt (speaker embedding + in-context codec tokens) once and reuse it: `hype` rows use the excited
  reference, `warm` rows the owner's own.
- Render N seeded takes per row on eris at the highest precision that fits; score word accuracy (Whisper) and speaker similarity; the
  best-scoring take is the candidate; the owner's ear later overrides any pick.
- Copy comes from A00's sheet; spoken names stay out (R69).
- Export picked takes as self-hosted **Ogg/Opus**, loudness normalised. **Apple hosts:** if A03 finds a clip doesn't decode in Safari/iOS Web
  Audio, the export writes an **AAC (`.m4a`) twin** from the same master.
- Regeneration is one command from the cue sheet; an audition reel exists; `manifest.json` records scores, seeds, model, dtype.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: A00's sheet and loader. Provides: voice clips + manifest to A03.

## Required tests
- The render command's automatic screens (WER, speaker similarity, loudness) per row, recorded in `manifest.json`; the loader rejection path from A00.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
`manifest.json` (scores, seeds, model, dtype) + the audition reel (`on:eris`). Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-A01/`.

- [x] [ev:ci] Regeneration is one command from the cue sheet.

- [x] [ev:ci] The `jammers-audio` skill exists, derived from `tools/audio/README.md`.

comments.author: GentlePike
comments.text: Announcer clips rendered and screened; owner listens at the checklist

comments.author: ChartreuseAspen
comments.text:
Owner direction (2026-10-03): encode once, from the processed raw master; the owner calls converting exported outputs far less efficient.
- export_clip() in tools/audio/voice_render_eris.py re-encodes Opus up to 8 times per clip (encode, decode, measure, adjust). Do the trim, gain and limiter on the float master and measure loudness on that lossless file, iterating there. Then encode Ogg/Opus once and decode it once for the export screen; re-encode only if that screen fails.
- The audition reel decodes the exported .ogg clips and re-encodes them (lossy to lossy). Build it from the processed masters instead.
- Keep the m4a twin encoding from the master, as it does now.

description:

## Purpose and observable outcome

## Scope (owned paths)

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Engine/crash SFX and the full AudioDirector (Full).

## Contract and design decisions
- Gesture unlock; lobby/intermission and race music; an announcer cue for every moment in A00's cue sheet, fired by the event the sheet names,
  picking among its variants without an immediate repeat; the sheet's **caption** for every cue (placed per the accepted TV mocks); one mix
  for the shared screen; denied/failed audio never blocks the round.
- **Audio on Apple hosts** (r3.6): the music (4a0f761) and voice exports are Ogg/Opus; whether Safari and iOS decode Ogg/Opus in Web Audio is
  unverified, and phone hosts (R08) and a Mac Safari host are in scope. Run the cue round in the **iOS Simulator lane (F08)** and **Playwright
  WebKit** and check every shipped clip decodes there. If any doesn't, the export writes an AAC (`.m4a`) twin (A01) and the host picks one per
  browser with `canPlayType`.
- Introspection (R90): a cue trigger log (which clip played, mix state) through the F05b surface.

title: P1-A04 · Engine synth prototype for the design review
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-A04** (cites master §14; owner 2026-10-03); master cut V2-92 slice (owner 2026-10-03) (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `POC` · **Track:** `audio` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** none; can start immediately.

## Purpose and observable outcome
A procedural engine sound the owner can hear and steer at the design review (owner 2026-10-03: "engine synth … I can review in my early
design review"), so the cars aren't silent in Playtest 1. The in-game version is P1-A05.

## Scope (owned paths)
`art/ui/poc/audio/engine/` (gallery page), `web/shared/audio/engine-synth/` (the synth as a reusable module), `assets/audio/engine/cruz-missile.json` (profile as data).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Wiring it to the sim and mixing many cars (P1-A05); announcer and music (A00–A03).

## Contract and design decisions
- Web Audio, no runtime CDN; procedural first (samples optional if the owner prefers them later).
- Layers driven by state: firing frequency from RPM (`rpm/60 × cylinders/2` with harmonics), intake/exhaust noise, throttle load, gear-change
  dips, a boost whine, drift tyre squeal (filtered noise), surface rumble (tarmac, dirt, gravel), and a damage rattle when parts are loose.
- Per-car profile as versioned data (the Cruz Missile: a small 4-cylinder with a cheeky exhaust).
- Gallery page: sliders for RPM, throttle, boost, surface and damage, plus a scripted lap that plays a recorded speed/throttle curve, so the
  owner hears it on the TV and a phone. Its CPU cost per voice is measured.

## Interfaces
- Provides: the synth module + profile to A05; the gallery page to U04.

## Required tests
- An offline render of the scripted lap is deterministic for the same input curve; per-voice CPU cost measured; the page works offline.

description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-C02** (cites §11, §5.4; master §4.2); master cut V2-11 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).

## Purpose and observable outcome
The phone controller players actually hold: two big sticks (DRIVE left, ACTION right, R60), secondary buttons away from thumbs, indicators,
touch hygiene, wake lock, portrait and landscape, built to the accepted POC phone mocks. No world renderer or sim on this route.

## Scope (owned paths)
`web/controller/src/` (sticks, buttons, HUD, wake lock).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Join/claim/resume and controller states (C03), scanner (C04), tutorial (C06), settings (C07), identity flash (R06).

## Contract and design decisions
- **Layout** (§11): two big floating sticks (fixed optional), DRIVE left, ACTION right. Secondary buttons away from thumbs: Identify, camera
  (chase/first person), Recover, Help, Settings, Leave. **Identify is also the first entry in the controller menu** (owner, 2026-10-03), and
  pressing it flashes the player's number full-screen in their colour on the phone while the TV shows the same (R06). Indicators next to the sticks: boost meter, wheelie preload, utility ready/cooldown.
- **Touch hygiene:** `touch-action: none`, no pinch/double-tap zoom, no text selection, no pull-to-refresh, safe areas, portrait and landscape.
  Stick zones start **≥ 24 px from the screen edges** (iOS Safari's edge swipe navigates back and CSS can't stop it).
- **Wake lock** while driving; re-requested on `visibilitychange`; vibration where supported (iOS has none, fine).
- Sends `StateBatch` records via `jj-wasm-input` (N06) over the `state` channel and `Action`s over `cmd` (N05); HUD from the state channel.
- Controllers load **no** world renderer or sim (bundle check in CI).
- A small connection badge shows how the controller is connected (direct or relay, reconnecting); P1-C08 reuses it (owner 2026-10-03).
Built to the accepted POC set (`art/ui/accepted/<date>/`, P1-U04); captures are judged against the matching accepted screen by a fresh-eyes review note (§13b.4: images opened at gameplay size, named reference, elements present/absent/ambiguous, first-look reading, defects, before/after per repair). title: P1-C03 · Join, claim and resume flow
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-C03** (cites §5.5, §9, §11; master §6.5); master cut V2-116a, V2-120 part (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D1` · **Track:** `ctrl` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-C02, P1-N07a, P1-S02, P1-F08, P1-U04. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Get a phone from a QR or a typed code to "You're #12" and keep it there through phone locks, Wi-Fi drops, reloads and duplicate tabs, with
every §11 controller state worded and reachable. Owns the curated prefill-name list.

## Scope (owned paths)
`web/controller/src/join/` (+ `web/controller/src/join/names.json`).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The seat reducer (N07a), scanner (C04), settings (C07).

## Contract and design decisions
Controller states (plan §11; C03 owns them; wording follows experience direction §3). Every failure names the next useful action and never shows a credential:
| State | When | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| Finding the game | code entered or join link opened | "Finding game K7QX…" |
| No such game | `not-found` on a fresh join | "No game with code K7QX": edit the code, scan again |
| Game ended | `ended`, or `Ended` received | "That game has ended" + final standings if received ("Thanks for playing" on Disband) |
| Preview expired | `410 {reason: preview-expired}` from the edge | "This test build has expired" + link to the index; not shown as an ended room |
| Connecting | registered, ICE in progress | "Connecting…" |
| Finding a relay | relay fallback requested or `429` | "Finding a relay…", retrying on its own |
| No route | no direct path and no relay left (`503`) | "Can't reach the host from this network. Try the host's Wi-Fi", plus Retry |
| Ready to join | connected, no seat | name field + **Join the race** |
| Joining | `Claim` sent | "Joining…" until `Welcome` |
| Playing | seated | "You're #12", sticks, Identify; READY in Lobby |
| Reconnecting | link lost, room `available` or `host-unreachable` < 2 min | "Reconnecting as #12…" (the car is on autopilot) |
| Host gone | `host-unreachable` ≥ 2 min, or `not-found` for the room it was seated in | "The host seems to have gone. Ask them for a new code" (keeps retrying quietly) |
| Host paused | host pause reason `host-hidden` | "Host paused, back in a moment" |
| Another tab | fenced by a newer tab | "Playing in another tab" + **Use this one** |
| Update needed | `ClaimRejected{build}` | reloads once |

- §5.5: endpoint id + secret in `localStorage`, namespaced by realm **and room**; entries for rooms reported `ended`/`not-found` are pruned;
  memory-only storage still plays and is told resume may not survive. Opening a URL never claims a seat; **Join the race** sends `Claim{requestId}`;
  "Joining…" until `Welcome`; then "You're #12" + Identify. Reconnect sends `Hello{resume}` → same seat, car, progress and score.
- Leave / Sit out with confirmation (master §10.6a: personal confirmation while driving).
- **Names** (§9): prefilled fun Aussie name, editable (≤ 32 graphemes, text only, NFC, duplicate-suffix rules). The prefill comes from a small
  curated, family-friendly list as data (`names.json`, a family-friendly flag per row). The full generator with reroll stays V2-112 (Full).
- The edited name is **remembered per device and realm** and prefilled next time (master V2-79a0 "remembered selection"); storage denied
  still plays with the honest note.
- The §11 **edge-swipe guard**: a `history.pushState` guard keeps an accidental back gesture on the controller; resume covers anything that slips.
Built to the accepted POC set (`art/ui/accepted/<date>/`, P1-U04); captures are judged against the matching accepted screen by a fresh-eyes review note (§13b.4: images opened at gameplay size, named reference, elements present/absent/ambiguous, first-look reading, defects, before/after per repair). A fixture screenshot never claims a gameplay pass.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: C02, N07a, S02 (real host), F08. Provides: join/resume to G04, C04, G03 (JN6), Q02 (recovery row).

## Required tests
Playwright: page hidden for 30 s with its network cut, then shown → same seat within 3 s; reload → same seat; a second tab fences the first; a
lost `Claim` response retried with the same `requestId` yields one seat; each §11 state reached by a scripted cause (unknown code, ended room,
expired-preview `410`, relay `429` then `503`, host gone, host hidden, fenced tab, protocol mismatch) shows its wording. F08: on both emulators a
background → foreground cycle returns the same seat within 3 s.

In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Playwright output. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-C03/`.

title: P1-C05 · Host pads and keyboard sources
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-C05** (cites §11, §13b.6; master §4.3); master cut V2-12 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).

## Purpose and observable outcome
Gamepads and keyboard clusters on the host as first-class players: claim-by-press, the same `jj-input` interpretation as phones, an input
drawer, and clean per-source dropout. On the critical path (… S02 → C05 → M02 …): the procgen spike drives through biomes with keys or a pad.

## Scope (owned paths)
`web/host/src/input/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Phones (C02). The input drawer's visual design (accepted TV mocks, R07).

## Contract and design decisions
- Gamepad API + key clusters → `LocalSource{sourceId, axes, buttons, seq}` (§4.4), already sampled; the worker interprets them with the same
  `jj-input` path as phones (source-blind DriveIntent).
- **Claim-by-press** creates a seat (no phantom seats); the input drawer lists sources.
- The **key-cluster map is data** (two-stick per cluster). Host commands (the §13b.6 bug-clip chord Ctrl/⌘+Shift+B, host UI) never use a
  cluster key.
- A pad's View/Select is its **Identify**; its Start is its **READY**. Each key cluster has its own **Identify** key and **READY** key in the
  cluster map (owner, 2026-10-03), shown in the input drawer's key legend.
- Every local seat can **Leave** or **Sit out** like any seat (plan §9), at a tick boundary with standings kept (DEFAULT: hold the pad's
  View/Select + Start for 2 s, or the cluster's equivalent keys, or use the input drawer); the same source can claim a seat again later
  (owner, 2026-10-03: any controller can join the lobby and optionally leave).
- Each disconnected pad is reported independently even while other sources continue (master §4.4); digital steering has rate shaping.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: S02, N06, N07a. Provides: local sources to M02 (spike drive), G04 (key cluster journey), F10 (emulated pads), N08 receipt format.

Playwright with an emulated Gamepad API and key events: two pads + two key clusters claim four seats and each drives only its own car;

title: P1-C07 · Personal controller settings
description:

## Purpose and observable outcome
Per-device controller preferences (stick placement, response curve, vibration, reduced motion) remembered per realm, with honest behaviour
when storage is denied, and a settings menu that safely hands the car to autopilot while it's open.

## Scope (owned paths)
`web/controller/src/settings/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The host-side autopilot handoff (checked end to end in P1-G03).

## Contract and design decisions
Master §10.6a: a versioned `ControllerPreferences` record per browser origin, production/preview namespace and local source profile: layout
(floating default / fixed), approved response preset (monotonic over the full range; never changes force, speed, brake authority or stunt
thresholds), haptics, motion, preferred camera; never seat grants, votes, Ready or scores. "Remember on this device" defaults on; off = apply
in memory only and remove any saved record. **Reset controls** restores defaults after confirmation. Storage failure applies for this session
and says "Applied for now — this browser couldn't remember your settings". Unknown/invalid values use visible defaults. Missing haptics
disables that toggle with a reason. Opening Settings/Help sends neutral and `Menu{open:true}`; closing (Save or Cancel/Back) requires all
controls neutral, sends `Menu{open:false}` and never fires a wheelie, boost or utility; reclaim only on later deliberate input.

description:

## Purpose and observable outcome
Explicitly support more players than phones (owner 2026-10-03): a second laptop with 3–4 pads, a laptop with just a keyboard, or a phone with
a paired pad, each joining as one controller endpoint that carries several players, with a small UI showing how each controller is connected.

## Scope (owned paths)
`web/controller/src/hub/` (the `/hub` route), `web/shared/input/` (pad/key mapping shared with C05), `web/shared/ui/connection-badge/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Host-local pads and keys (C05); real-device rows (P1-Q02 checklist).

## Contract and design decisions
- `B/hub` (and the phone controller with a paired pad, R65): one WebRTC connection, two channels, sources batched fairly into `StateBatch`
  (§5.4: split by ~1,000 bytes or 255 records, never truncated); per-source freshness, and **each unplugged pad reported independently** while
  the others keep playing (R80).
- **Each source joins and leaves on its own:** a pad press or key cluster claims its own seat (number, colour, name); View/Select (pads) or the
  cluster's Identify key is Identify, flashing that source's row on the hub in its colour while the TV shows the number; Start or the
  cluster's READY key is READY; a hold chord leaves.
- **Connection UI:** the hub lists every source with its seat number and colour, kind (pad, keys, touch), state (connected, unplugged,
  autopilot) and the connection path (direct or relay, RTT). The phone controller shows the same small badge (direct/relay/reconnecting).
- Sources are a test sample, never a limit (R66).

## Required tests
- Playwright with emulated Gamepad API + key events: a hub page with four pads and two key clusters → six seats over one connection.
- Unplug one pad → only its seat neutralises and goes to autopilot; the UI shows it unplugged.
- A phone page + one emulated paired pad → two seats.
- Payload/wire bytes and input age per source in the N08 receipt format.

title: P1-D01 · Gitea primary, GitHub mirror, Jammers runners
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-D01** (cites §4.2, §12.1); master cut V2-08 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D0` · **Track:** `deploy` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:deploy-repo`, `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-F01. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Make Gitea the primary home for 0.2 (R18): create the two repos with `tea`, push `v0.2-revamp` there, mirror to GitHub, get the shared
runners building with a warm cargo cache, and give agents `scripts/ci-status.sh --wait` so nobody queries Gitea by hand. The deploy
trust boundary is where the **secrets** live (`jammers-deploy`), not which runner executes.

## Scope (owned paths)
Gitea repo settings (created with `tea`, login `gitea-lan`: `multiplayer-racer` and `jammers-deploy`), `.gitea/workflows/`, `scripts/ci-status.sh`, `docs/deploy/README.md`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The preview edge (D03), publish workflows (D04), image build (D02). Production 0.1 keeps deploying from GitHub `main` as it does now.

## Contract and design decisions
- Two Gitea repos, one monorepo (§4.2): game code, art, tools, docs in `cdilga/multiplayer-racer` (primary on Gitea, passive mirror on GitHub);
  `jammers-deploy` holds deploy workflows, deploy secrets, smoke steps, the preview register, the edge config and the `turn-broker`
  deployment. Why: in Gitea Actions a workflow a pushed branch can edit can read that repo's secrets, and agents push candidate branches
  all day. On the Mac, `jammers-deploy` has exactly one checkout at `../jammers-deploy`; same rules (one shared tree, Agent Mail reservations
  under its own project key, no clones/worktrees).
- Gitea at `http://192.168.11.12:3001`. Today this tree's only remote is GitHub `origin`; add Gitea as the remote agents and the verifier push
  to, leave `main` and production 0.1 deploying from GitHub, set the GitHub push mirror on Gitea.
- **LFS on Gitea** (the repo uses LFS for `art/**` and `spikes/**`; `git push` doesn't upload LFS: run `git lfs push --all <remote> <branch>`).
- **Shared runners** across all the owner's projects (owner 2026-10-02, deploy runners included): any runner still scoped to one repo (e.g.
  Physical Soccer's TrueNAS Rust runner with its persistent cargo cache: warm Rust jobs 23–32 s vs 168 s cold) is re-registered as shared;
  Linux runners for Playwright lanes; triton's GPU runner (GTX 1080) as a headed 4K perf lane.
- Images go to the Gitea package registry; **no GitHub Actions and no GHCR** for 0.2.
- CI lanes: fast (fmt, clippy, `cargo test`, goldens, no-Tokio, web type/lint), build (WASM + web bundles + `jj-server` image), browser
  (Playwright host + controller over loopback WebRTC, no-CDN cold-cache check), and the public smoke on publish.
- `scripts/ci-status.sh --wait` reports every lane for HEAD (exit 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 pending). Gitea CI runs on the verifier's once-per-wave push.

## Interfaces
- Provides: Gitea remote + CI lanes + registry to D02/D03/D04; `ci-status.sh` to the coordinator and verifier.

## Required tests
- A push to Gitea `v0.2-revamp` and a second push with no Rust change; a clean clone fetching LFS from Gitea; `ci-status.sh --wait`.

title: P1-D03 · Preview edge at `jammers-preview.dilger.dev`
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-D03** (cites §12.2, §3a); master cut V2-31 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).

**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-D01, P1-D02. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Route `jammers-preview.dilger.dev/p/<id>/` to per-preview `jj-server` containers, serve the index at `/` and keep serving the design POC at
`/poc/`, as TrueNAS apps managed through the middleware so the edge survives TrueNAS reboots without hand-fixing.

## Scope (owned paths)
`jammers-deploy` repo: edge config, compose/app definitions.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Publishing (D04), index content (D05), retention (D06).

## Contract and design decisions
- One preview origin; each preview at `/p/<id>/` with **its own backend container** (its own `jj-server`, rooms and secrets). Production
  `jammers.dilger.dev` stays 0.1 until 0.2 promotion.
- `<id>` is an **immutable deployment id**, one per publish, never reused (DEFAULT `<branch-slug>-<short-sha>`, plus a suffix if the same
  commit is published again); "Latest" and "Playtest 1" are labels in the register pointing at ids.
- Edge router: DEFAULT Traefik or Caddy with per-container routes; pick whatever survives TrueNAS reboots without hand-fixing (the
  docker-group drop broke 0.1's compose deploy). A **TrueNAS app managed through the middleware (`midclt`)**, never an ad hoc `docker compose`
  stack. Runs behind the existing Cloudflare Tunnel route (live since 2026-10-02 with the placeholder app `jammers-preview-edge` on `:30290`,
  which this replaces). Keeps serving `/poc/` (§3a). SSE passes through **unbuffered**.
- Every asset, worker, WASM fetch and API call uses the base path; root-relative requests that could leak to another preview fail.
- **No agent reboots the NAS** (it takes down Home Assistant, cameras and Gitea). Prove recovery by stopping and starting the apps through
  the middleware; the real reboot is observed in an owner-approved window (O11, not a gate).

## Interfaces
- Consumes: D01 (repos/runners), D02 (image). Provides: routing + `/poc/` to U04, D04, D05, D06, N02's real-tunnel SSE check.

## Required tests
- Two previews of the same build side by side; a 5-minute SSE stream through tunnel + edge; middleware stop/start test.

## Acceptance

## Evidence

description:
**Source:** owner direction 2026-10-03 (stream POC updates as early as possible, via CI/CD); plan §3a delivery. **Drop:** `POC` · **Track:** `deploy` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`

Every push that touches `art/ui/poc/` is live at `https://jammers-preview.dilger.dev/poc/` within a minute, with no manual step, through Gitea CI (`.gitea/workflows/poc-deploy.yml` -> `scripts/poc-publish.sh`). The owner starts G-DESIGN feedback now rather than after D01-D04. Every later POC bead (rework from U01-U03/U05, new mocks) ships by committing, not by a hand deploy.

`.gitea/workflows/poc-deploy.yml`, `scripts/poc-publish.sh`; the preview edge's `/srv/poc` bind mount (system-administration `jammers-preview-edge/build_app_payload.py`); the `POC_DEPLOY_KEY` Gitea secret.

title: P1-D04 · Publish previews with smoke
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-D04** (cites §12.3, §3); master cut V2-30 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).

**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-D01, P1-D03, P1-G00. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Every candidate that passes CI publishes a preview automatically (R85: no freeze; the playtest is a pinned preview). The first published
preview is the G00 walking skeleton. The game repo holds no credential that can start or shape a deploy.

## Scope (owned paths)
`jammers-deploy` workflows (triggered by green CI), smoke steps + verifier script.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Index page (D05), retention/pinning (D06), the full mandatory smoke (D07).

## Contract and design decisions
- **Trigger (DEFAULT):** `jammers-deploy` polls on a schedule (every 5 min, plus manual dispatch) with a read-only token held only there,
  lists green CI runs on the game repo and publishes any it hasn't seen.
- The workflow verifies the candidate's **digest and CI status**, starts its backend as a middleware-managed TrueNAS app, waits for health,
  runs the public smoke, then adds the index row. A failed smoke leaves the row marked "not playable" with the reason.
- **Fixed scripts only:** the candidate can't supply deploy commands. The bundle carries a `smoke.json` naming which of a **fixed** set of
  smoke steps it supports (data, never commands): `room`, `join-webrtc`, `input`, `resume`, `drive`, `hud`, `round`. G00 declares `room`,
  `join-webrtc`, `input`, `resume`. An unknown step name fails the publish. The smoke drives its own headless host page with the test flag
  and reads state through that host's test surface (previews are test-enabled builds; production never is).
- Secrets scoped to the deploy repo; the game repo's secret listing shows only the CI registry push token.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: D01, D03, the G00 build and its `smoke.json`. Provides: the publish pipeline to D05/D06/D07 and every later preview.

## Required tests
- Three consecutive publishes via the scheduled poll; an unknown-step `smoke.json`; a cross-preview room-code resolve.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Three publish logs. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-D04/`.

title: P1-D06 · Retention reconciler, pin/unpin
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-D06** (cites §12.5; master §16.2a); master cut V2-31 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D5` · **Track:** `deploy` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:deploy-repo`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-D04, P1-D05. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Keep previews tidy without ever losing the pinned playtest build: hourly and on publish, apply R73's ordered policy; pin/unpin is a
`jammers-deploy` workflow; expired links explain themselves.

## Scope (owned paths)
`jammers-deploy` reconciler + schedule.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The index page itself (D05).

## Contract and design decisions
Ordered policy (R73, master §16.2a), hourly and on publish:
1. Owner-pinned previews survive until explicitly unpinned.
2. The latest preview survives regardless of age.
3. Other unpinned previews older than 24 hours expire.
4. Retain at most the three newest unpinned previews; pins are additional.
Idempotent; **preserves evidence before removal** (bug reports/owner feedback as evidence artefacts); stops/removes container, route and
disposable volume; retains the registry/evidence record. Pin/unpin is a workflow with the preview id as input (Gitea UI or `tea`).
An expired link shows an explanation and a link to the index, never a broken socket. API calls under an expired base path get
`410 {reason: preview-expired}` from the edge, so a controller still open on it says "This test build has expired" (§11).
The three-preview policy is explicitly authorised and unrelated to player caps.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: D04's register, D05's index. Provides: the 410 contract C03 shows.

## Required tests
- A scripted sequence of publishes/pins/time skips against a test register; an expired link and an API call under it.

**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-D09** (cites master §16.4; deploy-topology); master cut V2-33 + V2-00b remainder (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `REL` · **Track:** `deploy` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:deploy-repo`, `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-D08. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
After 0.2 has run in production for a while, switch off what kept 0.1 alive and make the repo's front-door docs describe 0.2, so nothing old
misleads people or agents.

## Scope (owned paths)
`ppaas-workflows` 0.1 deploy (GHCR, docker-compose on TrueNAS), the Python game server app, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.claude/agents/`, project skill adapters.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)

## Contract and design decisions

  docker-compose deploy, the GHCR images and the `ppaas-workflows` path for this game; archive the last 0.1 image; keep the Python offline and
  Blender tools.
- Bring the remaining front-door docs in line with 0.2 (master V2-00b): `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.claude/agents/`, project skill
  adapters, CI/workflow docs; nothing live contradicts the owner-direction policy.

## Required tests
- Inventory before and after; a doc-consistency check (no live instruction contradicts the policy); the reconcile gate passes.

## Acceptance

## Evidence

- `ev:ci`: green Gitea CI on a commit containing this bead, cited as `receipt:<run url>` with a `batch_verify` gate pass (before CI exists, a committed local receipt; while CI is down, the verifier's `batch-verify.sh` receipt).

## Anti-narrowing clause

- [ ] [ev:deploy-repo] After the owner-confirmed window, the 0.1 production app, its compose deploy, GHCR images and the ppaas path are retired, with the last image archived and the offline tools kept.

title: P1-F01 · Rust workspace and web workspace scaffold
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-F01** (cites §4.2, §4.3, §15.2); master cut V2-01 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D0` · **Track:** `found` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** none; can start immediately.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Create the empty 0.2 workspace every other bead builds in: the Rust workspace with all thirteen crates as compiling stubs, the
`web/` npm workspace with Vite, the toolchain pins and the guards that keep the Mac's disk and the dependency graph healthy. The
0.2 code doesn't exist yet (the 0.1 code was removed from this branch, R87); this is the first code bead and it is on the
critical path (F01 → N01 → M01 → S01 → …).

## Scope (owned paths)
`Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `deny.toml`, `.cargo/config.toml`, `crates/*/` (empty crates with `lib.rs`/`main.rs`), `web/package.json`, `web/*/` skeletons, `.nvmrc` (repin), CI config stubs.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
CI runner setup and Gitea remotes (P1-D01); eris setup (P1-F06); the batch-verifier lanes (P1-F02); dependency qualification doc (P1-F03). The root `package.json` stays the spike/skills tooling manifest (three/Playwright for spikes) and must not be repurposed.

## Contract and design decisions
Repository layout to create (plan §4.2):
```text
Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain.toml, deny.toml   Rust workspace (stable toolchain)
crates/
  jj-types/        typed IDs, units, small math; no I/O
  jj-protocol/     wire formats: controller state/commands/HUD, signalling DTOs, worker ABI; goldens
  jj-input/        source shaping, DriveIntent, action detection (sectors, wheelie), scheduler
  jj-session/      host room reducer: seats, claims, resume, ready/start, round director, results
  jj-sim/          Rapier world, vehicle, damage parts, debris, race progress, placement, autopilot
  jj-map/          jj.map.v1 schema, canonical bytes, validator, loader (authored + generated)
  jj-procgen/      seeded generation -> jj.map.v1 (native + WASM)
  jj-contracts/    asset sidecar schemas + GLB validator (vehicle first)
  jj-wasm-host/    wasm-bindgen facade for the host sim worker (session + input + sim)
  jj-wasm-procgen/ wasm-bindgen facade for the procgen worker
  jj-wasm-input/   wasm-bindgen facade for controllers (input + protocol only)
  jj-server/       binary: static serving, rooms, signalling, ICE provider, health
  jj-tools/        CLI (`jj`): sim, procgen, validate (§13b.2); JSON output
web/
  package.json     npm workspaces; Vite; all deps bundled, no CDNs (R70)
  shared/          generated protocol bindings glue, transport (WebRTC + signalling), UI tokens
  host/            host app: render, worker glue, grid, HUD, lobby, reel
  controller/      controller app: sticks, HUD, join/resume, scanner (no Three.js)
  landing/         index page: HOST A GAME / JOIN A GAME
tools/vehicles/    bake: model script -> GLB + sidecar (Node, from Spike J)
tools/audio/       eris generation scripts and cue sheets (existing, R89)
assets/            versioned runtime data: profiles/, kit/ (kit-piece registry), audio/ (approved exports only)
maps/              authored maps in the human-editable jj.map.v1 JSON form (greybox-loop.json)
scenarios/         scenario-bank fixtures (feel/, damage/, race/, affordances/, ...); accepted/ baselines
docs/evidence/     per-bead evidence docs/evidence/<P1-ID>/
docs/learnings/    append-only traps and fixes per area
scripts/remote/    run a command on eris against the current tree
```

- Stable Rust pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target listed.
- One Node LTS pinned for `web/` and the repo root (replace the stale 18.20.8 `.nvmrc`).
- `.cargo/config.toml` and the workspace profile set `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` and a slim dev profile (line-tables-only debug info),
  because a local `target/` filled the Mac's disk on Physical Soccer. Workspace-wide cargo on the Mac is hook-blocked; per-crate
  local builds are fine within a 15 GiB `target/` budget.
- `cargo deny` (licences/advisories) and a **no-Tokio `cargo tree` check** (R2) wired as scripts the CI stubs and F02 call.
- npm workspaces with Vite; all deps bundled, no CDNs (R70).
- `jj-server` and `jj-tools` are binaries; `jj-wasm-*` crates are `cdylib` facades that must compile for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

## Interfaces
- Provides: the workspace to every crate/web bead; `rust-toolchain.toml` that P1-F06 installs on eris; the no-Tokio and
  `cargo deny` checks that P1-F02's `rust` lane runs.

## Required tests
- `rch exec -- cargo check --workspace` (native) and `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` for the `jj-wasm-*` crates.
- `npm --prefix web run build` on the Mac.
- The no-Tokio check demonstrated failing on a deliberately added Tokio dep (then removed).

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Command output. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-F01/`.

## How this bead closes
- `ev:ci`: green Gitea CI on a commit containing this bead, cited as `receipt:<run url>` with a `batch_verify` gate pass (before CI exists, a committed local receipt; while CI is down, the verifier's `batch-verify.sh` receipt).

## Working rules
Follow `AGENTS.md` (owner rules first) and `docs/process/bead-workflow.md`: check your own area, commit with `P1-F01` and the bead ID in the message, push, and close this bead once CI is green on a commit containing it (gate pass, ticked items, `receipt:<run url>`).

## Anti-narrowing clause
> Done only when the FELT, observable outcome above holds in the RUNNING game via the real host path. Passing unit/geometry tests is necessary but NOT sufficient.

- [x] [ev:ci] `rch exec -- cargo check --workspace` succeeds on a clean clone through the existing RCH worker (devbox until P1-F06 adds eris), natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` for the `jj-wasm-*` crates.
- [x] [ev:ci] `npm --prefix web run build` succeeds on the Mac.
- [x] [ev:ci] The no-Tokio check fails on a deliberately added Tokio dependency (output recorded), then passes once it is removed.
- [x] [ev:ci] `.nvmrc` and `web/` pin one Node LTS; `.cargo/config.toml` sets `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` and the slim dev profile.

comments.text: Commit 97f86b6 (pushed to origin; no Gitea repo until P1-D01). Local receipt: docs/evidence/P1-F01/local-receipt.txt, no-tokio demo: docs/evidence/P1-F01/no-tokio-demo.txt. title: P1-F02 · CI lanes, close rules and the verifier's local runner
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-F02** (cites §12.1, §13, §13.4, §15.0; docs/process/bead-workflow.md); master cut process (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D0` · **Track:** `found` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-F01, P1-D01. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Status notes
**Already done outside the tracker (2026-10-03):** Physical Soccer's close rules in `.beads/policy.yaml` (a session closes its own bead
with a `batch_verify` gate pass, a `receipt:` reference and every acceptance item ticked), the canary rewritten for them (28 checks, passing on
br 0.7.4), the hook cut to the Mac disk guard and `br delete`, and `docs/process/bead-workflow.md`. F02 keeps them in step and builds the rest.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Give every session an objective check to close on: the §13 lanes as Gitea CI on the shared runners (Physical Soccer's model, owner 2026-10-03:
sessions close their own beads once CI is green on a commit containing them), a local lane runner the verifier on call uses when CI is down or
not built yet, and the evidence close for owner verdicts, `jammers-deploy` work and hardware receipts.

## Scope (owned paths)
`.gitea/workflows/`, `scripts/beads/batch-verify.sh`, `scripts/ci-status.sh` (P1-D01 creates it; F02 adds lanes), `.beads/policy.yaml`, `.claude/hooks/worker-guard.sh`, `scripts/beads/canary.sh`, `docs/process/bead-workflow.md`, `docs/evidence/README.md` (evidence record schema), the evidence commit-msg hook.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Gitea repos, mirror, runners and the fast lane (P1-D01); the journey harness and milestone matrix (P1-F10).

## Contract and design decisions
**CI lanes** (§13 table) as Gitea workflows with path filters on the shared runners:
| Lane | Runs | Triggered by changes under |
|---|---|---|
| `rust` | fmt, clippy, `cargo test`, `jj-protocol` goldens, no-Tokio | `crates/**`, `Cargo.*` |
| `scenarios` | the scenario-bank `cargo test` targets | `crates/jj-sim/**`, `crates/jj-map/**`, `crates/jj-procgen/**`, `scenarios/**`, `maps/**`, `assets/profiles/**` |
| `wasm-parity` | designated crate tests under `wasm32-unknown-unknown` in Node via `wasm-bindgen-test-runner` (pinned with wasm-bindgen) | `crates/jj-wasm-*/**` and anything the scenarios lane triggers |
| `web` | build, type check, unit | `web/**` |
| `e2e` | Playwright smoke | `web/**` |
| `tools` | bake reproducibility, validators | `tools/**`, `art/vehicles/**` |
`scripts/ci-status.sh --wait` reports each lane for a commit (exit 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 pending). Gitea cancels superseded runs.

**Local lane runner** (the verifier on call; remove the 0.1 suites): `batch-verify.sh plan` picks the same lanes from a git range; `run` runs them
across RCH (devbox on triton, eris when on) and the Mac in parallel, with a revision-bound receipt (base, head, tree, dirty inventory, toolchain,
lockfile hashes, exact commands, exit codes, each lane's machine) and a short summary (pass/fail counts, failing assertions with file:line); full
logs in `.beads/receipts/logs/`. Compile gates first (an aborted compile can print a misleading green prefix). `close` closes a `batch_pending`
bead whose commits are in a green receipt or CI run.

**Evidence close** (§15.0): `batch-verify.sh close <id> --evidence <file>` validates a committed evidence record against
`docs/evidence/README.md` (bead ID, acceptance items covered, observer, date, build/preview id, or external commit range + CI run for
`ev:deploy-repo`) and closes with `receipt:<evidence file>`; manual evidence is never recorded as a suite pass. Evidence commit-msg hook (§13b.5):
reject changes to another bead's `docs/evidence/<ID>/` unless the message names it or says `Recapture:`.

**Bootstrap:** F01, D01 and F02 close on committed local receipts, since CI doesn't exist until they land.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: the workspace (F01); Gitea repos, runners and `ci-status.sh` (D01); the RCH pool (F06 when it lands).
- Provides: CI to every bead's close; the local runner and evidence close to the verifier on call; lane names F10's milestone matrix builds on.

## Required tests
- One push per lane case (protocol, sim, web, tools) with the CI lanes it triggered, and `batch-verify.sh plan` on the same ranges.
- A `run` + `close` of a `batch_pending` test bead; evidence-close rejection cases; the canary.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
CI run links for each case; plan and run output; canary output. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-F02/`.

## How this bead closes
- `ev:ci`: green Gitea CI on a commit containing this bead, cited as `receipt:<run url>` with a `batch_verify` gate pass (before CI exists, a committed local receipt; while CI is down, the verifier's `batch-verify.sh` receipt).

## Working rules
Follow `AGENTS.md` (owner rules first) and `docs/process/bead-workflow.md`: check your own area, commit with `P1-F02` and the bead ID in the message, push, and close this bead once CI is green on a commit containing it (gate pass, ticked items, `receipt:<run url>`).

## Anti-narrowing clause
> Done only when the FELT, observable outcome above holds in the RUNNING game via the real host path. Passing unit/geometry tests is necessary but NOT sufficient.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] [ev:ci] Pushes changing `crates/jj-protocol` (rust + wasm-parity), `crates/jj-sim` (rust + scenarios + wasm-parity), `web/` (web + e2e) and `tools/vehicles` (tools) run exactly those CI lanes, and `scripts/ci-status.sh --wait` reports them.
- [ ] [ev:ci] `batch-verify.sh plan` picks the same lanes locally for the same ranges.
- [ ] [ev:ci] A session closes its own test bead on a green CI run with the gate pass and a `receipt:<run url>`.
- [ ] [ev:ci] `batch-verify.sh run` produces a revision-bound receipt naming each lane's machine with a short summary, and `close` closes a `batch_pending` bead from it.
- [ ] [ev:ci] An evidence close rejects an uncommitted, malformed, wrong-bead or incomplete record and accepts a deploy-repo record with no game-repo commit.
- [ ] [ev:ci] The canary passes, including new checks for the evidence path; the evidence commit-msg hook rejects an unnamed change to another bead's evidence.

title: P1-F03 · Dependency qualification and self-hosted asset manifest
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-F03** (cites §4.3; R70); master cut V2-118 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D0` · **Track:** `found` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-F01. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Pin and qualify every dependency the playtest build ships, with version, features, licence, source and why, and list every
runtime origin the build talks to, so "no runtime CDNs" (R70) and "no Tokio" (R2) are checked facts rather than intentions.

## Scope (owned paths)
`docs/deps/qualification.md`, `Cargo.toml`, `web/package.json`, lockfiles.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The renderer backend decision (P1-R01 measures it); Asupersync's behaviour under load (P1-N02 qualifies its server).

## Contract and design decisions
Dependency pins to qualify (plan §4.3; numbers are starting evidence, not decisions):
| Dependency | Starting point | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Rust | current stable at P1-F01, pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` | Asupersync 0.5.0 built on stable 1.97.1 with `default-features = false, features = ["native-runtime", "tls-webpki-roots"]` in an unrelated project (idea-level evidence only, R1) |
| Asupersync | 0.5.0 (check for newer) | Has `http` (h1/h2 server + client), `tls`, `net`; SSE is a streamed `text/event-stream` body |
| rapier3d | 0.36.0 | Enable `enhanced-determinism`; verify the vehicle controller API (`update_vehicle`, wheel friction, brake = impulse) |
| wasm-bindgen | current stable | Pin the CLI to the crate version; same CLI version on the Mac and eris |
| Node | current LTS | Root `.nvmrc` says 18.20.8 (0.1 pin, EOL); the Mac runs 24 and eris 26. Repin one version everywhere |
| three | r186 or newer stable | WebGPURenderer vs WebGLRenderer decided in P1-R01 |
| Vite | current stable | Base path from config (`/p/<id>/` for previews) |
| QR decoder | bundled JS/WASM decoder + `BarcodeDetector` when present | Self-hosted (R70) |
| QR encoder | small bundled encoder for the host's join QR (G00, R07) | Self-hosted; no image service |
No Tokio in the shipping graph (R2): `cargo tree` check in CI. Lockfiles committed.

The manifest lists **every runtime asset/decoder served** and every runtime origin: only *self* and the configured STUN/TURN hosts
(`stun.cloudflare.com`, `turn.dilger.dev`, and Cloudflare TURN only via the lazy fallback, R92) are allowed.

## Interfaces
- Provides: pinned versions consumed by N02 (Asupersync), R01 (three), S01 (rapier3d), C04 (QR decoder), G00/R07 (QR encoder).

## Required tests
- `cargo deny check` (licences/advisories) output; build of the pinned set; a scripted origin scan of built bundles.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence

## How this bead closes

## Working rules
Follow `AGENTS.md` (owner rules first) and `docs/process/bead-workflow.md`: check your own area, commit with `P1-F03` and the bead ID in the message, push, and close this bead once CI is green on a commit containing it (gate pass, ticked items, `receipt:<run url>`).

## Anti-narrowing clause
> Done only when the FELT, observable outcome above holds in the RUNNING game via the real host path. Passing unit/geometry tests is necessary but NOT sufficient.

- [ ] [ev:ci] The pins resolve and build (native + wasm32 + web).

comments.author: GentlePike
comments.text:
Progress (GentlePike, d266c02): rapier3d 0.36.0 (enhanced-determinism) pinned + built native and wasm32 on eris; three 0.186.1 / uqr 0.1.3 / jsqr 1.4.0 pinned in web/ and built; cargo deny ok; origin scan in CI (web job) over web/dist + a qualification bundle, negative test fails on a planted CDN URL. docs/deps/qualification.md, docs/evidence/P1-F03/local-checks.txt.
BLOCKED (owner) for AC1: Asupersync 0.5.0's licence is MIT + an OpenAI/Anthropic rider (no rights to Anthropic or anyone acting on its behalf; 'use' includes executing/testing/analysing; no making it available to them). It conflicts with GPL-3.0 (no further restrictions) and with agents (Claude) building/testing it. R2 names Asupersync, so the agent didn't pin, build or read its source (only LICENSE). Unblock: owner decides (keep Asupersync and accept the licence position, e.g. a written permission from its author; or name another no-Tokio runtime for R2). Then pin it with default-features=false, features=[native-runtime, tls-webpki-roots], allow its licence in deny.toml if kept, and build.

comments.author: GentlePike
comments.text: AC2 (cargo deny) and AC3 (origin scan) green on Gitea CI: http://192.168.11.12:3001/cdilga/multiplayer-racer/actions/runs/999 (commit d266c02). AC1 waits on the Asupersync decision.

comments.author: ChartreuseAspen
comments.text:
OWNER DECISION (2026-10-03): the owner approves Asupersync's licence (MIT + the OpenAI/Anthropic rider) for R2, accepting the GPL-3.0 position. Unblocks AC1: pin it (default-features=false, features=[native-runtime, tls-webpki-roots]), allow its licence in deny.toml, build.
Safeguard recorded with the decision: the rider bars making the software available to Anthropic or anyone acting on its behalf, and counts analysing and testing as use. So Claude sessions treat Asupersync as an opaque dependency: cargo may build and link it, but no Claude session opens, reads, greps, pastes or summarises its source or docs. Work that needs its internals goes to a non-Anthropic worker (the OMP/GLM workers), or waits for written permission from its author.

comments.author: GentlePike
comments.text: Owner ruled (e85819b, R2): Asupersync's licence accepted; Claude sessions treat it as opaque (build/link only, never read source/docs); internals work goes to a non-Anthropic worker. GentlePike's attempt to pin it was refused by its session's safety classifier ('Untrusted Code Integration'), so the pin is handed to a non-Anthropic (OMP) worker or the owner. Recipe (resolution verified before the refusal): workspace Cargo.toml: asupersync = { version = "0.5.0", default-features = false, features = ["native-runtime", "tls-webpki-roots"] }; crates/jj-server/Cargo.toml: asupersync.workspace = true; deny.toml: [[licenses.exceptions]] for asupersync, franken-decision, franken-evidence, franken-kernel (their rider licence) and allow webpki-roots' licence (CDLA-Permissive-2.0, Mozilla's root list); then scripts/ci/no-tokio.sh, scripts/ci/deny.sh, a native cargo check of jj-server, and tick AC1 (AC2/AC3 already green, run 999).

title: P1-F04 · Plan↔bead reconciliation for P1 IDs
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-F04** (cites §15.0; BEAD-DEFINITION-OF-DONE.md); master cut V2-114 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D0` · **Track:** `found` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** none; can start immediately.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Guard against coverage drop (design → bead), the failure that lost ~35 0.1 feedback rows: a script that maps every §15 task ID
to bead IDs and fails on unmapped tasks or beads citing removed IDs, plus `scripts/plan-ref.sh` so agents read only the plan
block their bead names. Beads now carry `external_ref = P1-XXX`, which is what this reconciles on.

## Scope (owned paths)
`scripts/reconcile_plans_to_beads.py`, `scripts/reconcile_allowlist.txt`, `scripts/plan-ref.sh`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)

title: P1-F05a · Agent introspection foundation, native (R90)
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-F05a** (cites §13a, §13b.1, §13b.2, §13.3); master cut new (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D1` · **Track:** `found` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S01, P1-N07a. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
R90 requires every part of the game to be visible as data, settable, steppable/replayable and fixture-testable by agents. F05a turns
S01's bootstrap scenario runner and the session reducer into the **one shared native surface**, exposed as `jj sim`, so S03–S08,
M03 and later tasks extend it instead of inventing their own (plan T21). Observable outcome: with no browser, an agent loads the
greybox, spawns cars, claims seats, steps, reads state as JSON and replays to the same hash.

## Scope (owned paths)
Chosen by the implementer, e.g. `crates/jj-tools/src/probe/` plus a test-only command surface on the sim/session core; `jj sim` in `crates/jj-tools/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The browser-side surface (P1-F05b); `--sweep` (P1-S03 adds it); `--replay` of bug clips (P1-F07); `jj procgen` (P1-M03a); `jj validate` (P1-V01).

## Contract and design decisions
§13a capabilities for the sim and session core:
1. **See** state as structured JSON at a tick (cars: pose, velocity, speed, progress; seats: state, claims, source freshness).
2. **Set up** state directly (load map/fixture, spawn, place, claim seats, jump to a phase) without playing to it.
3. **Step** N ticks or until a predicate, deterministically; **replay** a recorded run.
4. **Assert** with a saved fixture (setup + inputs + expected observations/envelopes) that fails loudly printing what it observed.
Fixtures carry an **outcome signature** (§13b.1: the numbers that say what happened: yaw rate, slip, airtime, part states, travel,
recovery time, energy); envelopes are tolerances on signatures, not raw positions.

`jj` CLI rules (§13b.2): one small native binary with three commands (`sim`, `procgen`, `validate`); F05a builds `jj sim` with
`--trace` (one JSON row per tick: car poses, velocities, per-wheel contact/slip, inputs applied, part states, events) and `--compare RUN`
(an **ACCEPTED | CURRENT | TUNED** table against another run or the accepted baseline, §13.3). `--help` with worked examples; `--json`
on everything an agent parses; each run writes an evidence folder under `target/jj-runs/` (ignored) and exits non-zero with what it
observed on failure. One mechanism only: S01's runner becomes this surface (no second mechanism). Never reachable from production
controllers (master §15.1). Nothing changes sim state except journaled setup commands, so every run can be replayed (one sim funnel).

## Interfaces
- Consumes: `jj-sim` core, full-state hash, applied-tick journal and scenario format (S01); seat/claim reducer (N07a).
- Provides: the native introspection API and `jj sim` for S03–S08, S09, M03*, F05b (same JSON shapes in the browser), F07 (`--replay`).

## Reuses / gap
Reuses S01's scenario runner and journal; gap: no shared see/set/step/assert surface or trace/compare tooling.

## Required tests
- A scripted `jj sim --json` transcript doing the acceptance flow (greybox, three cars, three seats, 600 ticks, read, replay → same hash).
- A deliberately failing fixture showing the observed-vs-signature printout.
- `jj sim --trace` of `straight-throttle` on two commits fed to `jj sim --compare` showing the differing keys.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
A scripted `jj sim --json` transcript + hash match + one compare table. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-F05a/`.

title: P1-F05b · Agent introspection in the browser host (R90)
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-F05b** (cites §13a, §13b.2, §12.3); master cut new (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D1` · **Track:** `found` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-F05a, P1-S02. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
The F05a commands through the sim worker to Playwright (and to an agent driving a headed browser), with harness helpers on top, so
journeys, captures, the public smoke and agents can see and step the real host. Available in local runs and previews (test-enabled),
never in production, never reachable from controllers.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-wasm-host/` (test surface), `web/host/src/testing/` (a separate lazily loaded host chunk).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Journey harness (P1-F10), bug clips (P1-F07), perf helper policy (P1-Q01 uses it).

## Contract and design decisions
- The same JSON shapes as native (F05a), through the worker ABI's test-only messages, which exist only in test-enabled hosts (§4.4).
- **Availability (§13a DEFAULT):** the surface lives in a separate lazily loaded host chunk. A host page loads it only with the test
  flag in its URL, and only when the server's realm isn't `production`; a `production` realm serves no test chunk at all (404).
  Controllers have no path to it: the `cmd` channel carries no test messages, and the surface acts only on the page that loaded it.
  Bundle checks assert the main host and controller bundles contain no test code.
- Harness helpers (not CLI commands, §13b.2): blocking `until(predicate)` steps that wait on their own fact; a **capture helper** that
  records metadata (commit, asset/map hashes, fixture, seed, viewport, browser + backend); a **debug overlay** (per-wheel compression,
  slip and contact, damage episodes, part states) captures can switch on.
- **Paused and frame-stepped by default in test mode**, so an agent can look without losing its place.
- Guardrails live in the tool: test-only helpers refuse production URLs.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: F05a native surface; S02's worker and ABI.
- Provides: the browser test surface to F07, F10, G00-onward journeys, D04/D07 smoke (reads state through it), C06, A03, R-captures.

## Required tests
- Playwright: load host, spawn three cars through the surface, step the paused sim 600 ticks, read the same state hash the native run
  produced for the same fixture.
- Helper session: join three fake controllers, drive one until a predicate holds, write its evidence folder.
- Bundle checks + realm checks (production 404, preview serves, no URL flag → never loaded).

## Acceptance

## Evidence

title: P1-F06 · Compute fabric: every machine as a worker (§15.2, R93)
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-F06** (cites §15.2; R93); master cut new, process (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D0` · **Track:** `found` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-F01. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Use every machine with spare CPU (owner R93, 2026-10-03): register eris as an RCH worker beside devbox, move devbox's build storage onto
triton's big pool (devbox is a VM on triton), set eris up for browsers and the Android emulator, and keep the Mac's own CPU in play within its disk budget. Editing,
`br`, Agent Mail and commits stay on the Mac (one source of truth). Speed lever #1 in §15.2. eris is intermittent (guest bedroom), so
everything falls back to devbox through RCH or to the Mac.

## Scope (owned paths)
`scripts/remote/eris.sh`, `docs/process/dev-topology.md`, `scripts/reclaim-target.sh`, `scripts/prune-caches.sh`; machine setup on eris and devbox, RCH worker config, `ru` on eris (no repo files).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Batch-verifier lane routing (P1-F02 calls this); CI runners on Gitea (P1-D01); the emulator lane itself (P1-F08).

## Contract and design decisions
Machines (plan §15.2): the Mac (M1 Pro, 16 GB, disk 83 % full), eris (x86_64, 12 threads, 31 GB, RTX 2080 SUPER shared with audio jobs,
intermittent), devbox (the RCH worker today: a VM on triton, 20 threads, ~35 GB free disk), triton (devbox's host and a Gitea runner, GTX 1080, ZFS pool `tank`
10.9 TB with 5 TB free; resilvering and degraded on 2026-10-03, ~3 days left), the shared Gitea runners on TrueNAS.
- **RCH workers:** add **eris** beside devbox (today `rch workers` lists only devbox), so concurrent builds spread across them.
- **devbox storage:** once triton's resilver finishes and the pool is healthy, move devbox's `target/` and caches onto triton's pool so devbox stops
  running at 92 % disk. Don't load the pool while it's resilvering.
On eris:
- user-local **rustup** (leaves Arch's system `rust` package alone) honouring `rust-toolchain.toml`; the `wasm32` target; the pinned
  `wasm-bindgen-cli`; the pinned Node via mise; Playwright browsers (Chromium + WebKit).
- Playwright browsers and an **Android emulator** (x86_64 AVD with KVM) so the F08 lane can use eris when the Mac is busy.
- **Repo sync with `ru`** (Jeffrey Emanuel's Repo Updater, owner 2026-10-03): eris keeps a clean clone of each repo at `~/Work/dev/<repo>`
  (`ru` config on eris: `PROJECTS_DIR=~/Work/dev`, `LAYOUT=flat`, `UPDATE_STRATEGY=ff-only`; repos `cdilga/multiplayer-racer@v0.2-revamp`, and
  `jammers-deploy` once P1-D01 creates it). The existing clone at `~/Work/dev/multiplayer-racer` becomes the ru-managed one (keep any untracked
  files and report them; never delete). Agents **never edit on eris**: code changes happen only in the Mac's tree and reach eris as pushed
  commits. `ru` installed on eris at the same version as the Mac's.
- `scripts/remote/eris.sh <cmd>` runs `ru sync` for the repo on eris, checks eris's `HEAD` equals the Mac's `HEAD` (refusing with a clear
  message when the Mac has unpushed commits: push first), then runs the command in the clone and streams output back. `--run <id>` per-run
  directories (`~/Work/runs/<id>`) hold only **non-code** things: outputs, evidence, browser profiles, server state. Uncommitted Rust work
  doesn't need this: RCH ships the working tree to its worker itself. No other checkout, clone or worktree of the code exists on any machine.
- The Mac: per-crate local builds, Vite, Playwright and emulators use its CPU within the 15 GiB `target/` budget (the only Mac rule is
  disk: no workspace-wide cargo locally).
- `scripts/reclaim-target.sh` keeps the Mac's local `target/` under 15 GiB (prunes incremental and stale lane dirs);
  `scripts/prune-caches.sh` keeps eris's remote caches bounded. Perf or "looks" numbers from eris only when no audio job holds its GPU, labelled.
- Nobody reboots eris to test anything; a natural reboot is noted in the evidence when it happens.

## Interfaces
- Provides: the RCH worker pool and `scripts/remote/eris.sh` to F02 (lanes fan out), every worker's dev loop, F08 (Android emulator on eris), N05/N08 (local coturn container), D02 (image build).

## Required tests
- Command transcripts from each machine covering each acceptance item.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Command output from each machine. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-F06/`.

## How this bead closes
- `ev:ci`: green Gitea CI on a commit containing this bead, cited as `receipt:<run url>` with a `batch_verify` gate pass (before CI exists, a committed local receipt; while CI is down, the verifier's `batch-verify.sh` receipt).

## Working rules
Follow `AGENTS.md` (owner rules first) and `docs/process/bead-workflow.md`: check your own area, commit with `P1-F06` and the bead ID in the message, push, and close this bead once CI is green on a commit containing it (gate pass, ticked items, `receipt:<run url>`).

## Anti-narrowing clause
> Done only when the FELT, observable outcome above holds in the RUNNING game via the real host path. Passing unit/geometry tests is necessary but NOT sufficient.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] [ev:ci] `rch workers` lists devbox and eris; `rch exec -- cargo check --workspace` runs on each with the pinned toolchain (receipts name the worker), and two concurrent builds land on different workers.
- [ ] [ev:ci] devbox's build storage lives on triton's pool (after its resilver) with room to spare (`df` output recorded).
- [ ] [ev:ci] `scripts/remote/eris.sh npx playwright --version` works.
- [ ] [ev:ci] `ru status` on eris shows `multiplayer-racer` in sync with the pushed branch, and `scripts/remote/eris.sh` runs `ru sync` first and refuses with a clear message when the Mac has unpushed commits.
- [ ] [ev:ci] Two agents' simultaneous runs use the same ru-synced clone with separate output dirs and don't clobber each other's outputs; nothing on eris is edited by hand.
- [ ] [ev:ci] Pruning removes idle run dirs; `reclaim-target.sh` brings the Mac's `target/` under 15 GiB.
- [ ] [ev:ci] The RCH worker comes back after a restart of its service with no manual steps (a natural eris reboot, if one happens, is noted; nobody reboots it to test).
- [ ] [ev:ci] When eris is off, the same commands fall back to devbox through RCH, or to per-crate local runs on the Mac.

title: P1-F07 · Bug clips and replay (§13b.6)
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-F07** (cites §13b.6, §13.3, §13.4, §4.4); master cut new (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).

## Purpose and observable outcome
Turn owner playtest findings into reproducible work: a host hotkey/button saves a **bug clip** (build, map, roster, full applied-input
journal, marked moment) that `jj sim --replay` re-simulates to the same end-state hash. Also writes the playtest-loop process doc
(round records, bug-bead template, probe-first rule, accepted baselines).

## Scope (owned paths)
`web/host/src/diagnostics/clip/`, `crates/jj-tools/` (`jj sim --replay`), `docs/process/playtest-loop.md`, `.gitattributes` (LFS pattern `*.jjclip`).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Filing bug beads (the coordinator does that); the accepted baseline itself (saved at P1-Q02 when the owner accepts feel).

## Contract and design decisions
- Trigger: a host hotkey **Ctrl/⌘+Shift+B** (a modifier chord no key cluster uses, P1-C05) or a diagnostics button, on any host
  (previews included; host-only; saves a local file).
- Clip contents: build id, map bytes hash + seed, roster, and the full applied-input journal from the start of the current host
  session (free drive) or round (once G01's rounds exist), plus the marked moment. File: `*.jjclip` (LFS pattern added).
- The journal comes from the **main thread's copy** (`Journal{bytes}` chunks streamed from the worker, §4.4), so the fault screen's
  **Save bug clip** works after a worker panic.
- `jj sim --replay CLIP` re-simulates natively (or WASM in Node when native/WASM identity doesn't hold, §7.2), reports the end-state
  hash and the state at the marked moment, with `--trace` rows (§13.3). A clip from a different build is refused with a clear message.
- `docs/process/playtest-loop.md`: the §13.4 loop (owner playtests → coordinator writes `docs/playtests/round-<date>.md` with numbered
  findings → a bead per finding with its clip/scenario → worker writes the probe first (fails with numbers), fixes, shows it passing;
  the probe joins the affordance bank or the journeys → when the owner accepts a build's feel, its affordance-bank `jj sim --trace`
  outputs are committed under `scenarios/accepted/<preview-id>/`; a regression against an accepted baseline fails unless the owner
  accepts the new feel); the round-record template; the bug-bead template (clip, preview id, what was seen, probe-first rule).

## Interfaces
- Consumes: F05b test surface, the G04 free-drive host, the worker's `Journal` stream.
- Provides: clips + `--replay` to every repair bead, G05 (a clip saved during JN4 replays), Q02 (accepted baseline step).

## Required tests

- Inject a worker fault; save from the fault screen; replay up to the fault's tick.
- A clip from another build is refused.

description:

## Purpose and observable outcome
Bring expert shader knowledge into the agents' toolkit before the in-world look is designed (U05) and built (R10, R12): vendor two reviewed,
MIT-licensed three.js skills and add a short project adapter that turns our comic look into concrete shader recipes.

## Scope (owned paths)
`.claude/skills/webgpu-threejs-tsl/`, `.claude/skills/threejs-aaa-graphics-builder/`, `.claude/skills/jammers-look/SKILL.md` (adapter).

The look itself (U05 designs it, R10 builds it, R12 adds effects).

## Contract and design decisions
- **Vendor, don't install.** Read every file first (supply chain), then copy the skill folders with their LICENSE and the source commit:
  `dgreenheck/webgpu-claude-skill` → `webgpu-threejs-tsl` (Daniel Greenheck, Three.js Roadmap; MIT; aligned with three r183+: TSL node
  materials, post-processing, GPU-compute particles, WGSL) and `majidmanzarpour/threejs-game-skills` → `threejs-aaa-graphics-builder` (MIT;
  shader/material cookbook, VFX, render polish, visual scorecard). Never run their installers (`npx skills add`, `install.sh`).
- **`jammers-look` adapter:** maps master §12.1/§12.1a to recipes in TSL (for WebGPURenderer, which also runs on its WebGL2 backend) with a GLSL
  route if P1-R01 picks WebGLRenderer: 2–3 tone toon ramp; ink outlines from screen-space edges on depth + normals + object ID, once in post;
  halftone in shadows; selective emissive bloom; the paint key (white atlas texels tint by `instanceColor`); sun-bleached grit; per-tile cost
  rules (effects scale with tile size; comic effects never cover identity or the road ahead). Points at the plan and the accepted U05 frames.

race, results, intermission, auto-next) with the greybox as the round map. Journeys JN2 and JN3 prove it end to end.

title: P1-M01 · `jj.map.v1`, validator, loader and greybox
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-M01** (cites §8.1, §8.2, §13, §14); master cut V2-55 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D1` · **Track:** `maps` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-N01. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
The single map format the game loads (authored and generated), its validator and loader (native + WASM with identical canonical bytes), the
kit-piece registry schema with the generic greybox pieces, and the **authored greybox loop** every driving preview uses until procgen lands.
On the critical path (N01 → M01 → S01).

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-map/`, `maps/greybox-loop.json`, `assets/kit/` (registry schema + `generic/`), `jj validate` support for maps.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Map rendering (R03), procgen (M03*), biome kit pieces (M04–M07, M09), in-world graphics pieces (R10).

## Contract and design decisions
`jj.map.v1` (plan §8.1, DEFAULT layout; one document for authored and generated maps, master §11.2):
- Header: version, generator id/version, seed, biome set, bounds, `refLapMs`, gameplay hash. `refLapMs` is authored for the greybox; for a
  generated track it's the route length ÷ 15 m/s (DEFAULT, TUNE), reported against the autopilot's lap time (M03g).
- Units: millimetres (`i32`) for positions, centimetres (`i16`) for heights.
- Terrain: heightfield (spacing, heights) + surface-ID grid (`u8`: tarmac, packed dirt, gravel, rock, off-track).
- Route: centerline polyline (point, width, bank, surface), checkpoint gates, start grid rule (start corridor of declared length/width/row
  spacing), recovery corridors.
- Features: `{kind, pose, params}` (jump + landing envelope, crest, whoops, creek dip).
- Dressing: `{kitPiece, pose, params, collides}`; `kitPiece` names an entry in the **kit-piece registry** (`assets/kit/<family>/*.json`: id,
  parameter schema, collider proxy, LOD rule), validated by `jj-map`; `jj-sim` reads collider proxies for `collides` dressing, the renderer
  builds code geometry per id.
- Props: initial dynamic props (cones, bins).
- **Canonical bytes** = `postcard` encoding of the validated struct with sorted collections; hash those. A human-editable JSON form loads
  through the same validator. Canonicalisation/rounding is specified before native/WASM fixtures (not serializer float formatting).
- Validator (structural, runs in the browser on every map): drivable width, barrier/wall thickness, reachable gates, landing envelopes, a start
  corridor of the declared length and width with clear rows at the declared spacing (placement does the rest for any N), camera clearance,
  bounds; rejects missing/unknown gameplay fields. A failing seed retries within the preparation deadline, then falls back to a conservative
  recipe (master §11.2a).

title: P1-M02 · G-PROCSPIKE: seeded generation on the real stack (owner reviews, non-blocking)
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-M02** (cites §8.3; master §11.5a); master cut V2-49 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
