## Purpose and observable outcome
A throwaway spike on the real stack that generates varied seeds in all four biomes at playtest scope, compares scatter and undulation
candidates side by side, drives a car through them, measures determinism and generation time, and **recommends** algorithms, parameter
surface and kit-piece format. Its recommendation is the default the core (M03c–g) adopts; the owner looks when convenient (O5) and a redirect
becomes rework on the M03 children. On the critical path.

## Scope (owned paths)
`spikes/procgen/` (throwaway; its own Cargo workspace or an excluded member, so nothing in `crates/` depends on it).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The procgen core (M03*): written from the findings, not the spike code.

## Contract and design decisions
- Generate varied seeds in **all four biomes** (town, rocks/Olgas, outback dirt, outback bitumen) at playtest scope (master §11.5a).
- Compare **plant-scatter** and **undulation** candidates side by side (e.g. Poisson-disc vs blue-noise vs clustered scatter; noise vs spline
  undulation), with captures.
- Drive the car through the results with keys or a pad (C05); record a drive through each biome.
- Report native/WASM **byte-determinism** and **generation time** against the budgets: generate + validate ≤ 1.5 s on the laptop, ≤ 4 s on a
  phone host (TUNE).
- Recommend algorithms, parameter surface and kit-piece format. **Owner feedback never blocks** (§15.0): M03c–g proceed on the recommendation.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: M01, S02, R02, R03, C05. Provides: the recommendation to M03c (undulation), M03e (scatter), M03f (biome trait/kit format).

- Spike evidence only: report with captures per biome/seed, recorded drives, determinism check, timings; a fresh-eyes review note that the recommendation follows from the evidence.

**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-M03g** (cites §8.1, §8.3, §13b.1; master §11.2a); master cut V2-50/50a (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D4` · **Track:** `maps` · **Machine:** `on:mac` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`, `ev:hardware`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-M03d, P1-M03e, P1-M03f, P1-S07. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Close the procgen core: validator integration, the conservative fallback recipe, and the seed bank with bot playtests per seed. This is the
epic's acceptance and it is on the critical path.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-procgen/src/validate/`, `scenarios/procgen/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The browser worker and round preparation (M08a).

## Contract and design decisions
- Validator integration (§8.1 rules); a failing seed retries within the preparation deadline, then falls back to a **conservative recipe**; no
  endless silent reroll (master §11.2a).
- Budget: generate + validate **≤ 1.5 s in WASM on the Mac** (`ev:hardware`).
- **Bot playtests** (§13b.1): for every seed in the bank the autopilot reports stuck windows (softlocks), lap-time spread, recoveries,
  out-of-bounds count, and `refLapMs` against the autopilot's lap; any softlock is flagged.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: M03d, M03e, M03f, S07 (autopilot). Provides: the validated core to M04–M07, M08a.

## Required tests
- Seed bank `scenarios/procgen/` (100 seeds); WASM timing on the Mac; autopilot laps three seeds; bot-playtest report.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Seed-bank report + timing receipt. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-M03g/`.

- `ev:hardware`: a perf/network receipt naming hardware, browser/backend, build and cohort, closed through the evidence close (`batch-verify.sh close <id> --evidence <file>`, P1-F02).

## Anti-narrowing clause
> Done only when the FELT, observable outcome above holds in the RUNNING game via the real host path. Passing unit/geometry tests is necessary but NOT sufficient.

title: P1-M08a · Procgen worker and round preparation
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-M08a** (cites §4.4 (round preparation flow), §8.3; master §11.2a); master cut V2-58 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D4` · **Track:** `maps` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-M03, P1-N07b, P1-R03, P1-S02. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Put the generator behind the round preparation flow in the browser: a procgen worker prepares the next map during intermission, the renderer
builds and uploads it, the sim commits it atomically, stale jobs never win, and reroll and failure are handled.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-wasm-procgen/`, `web/host/src/prepare/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The four-biome recipe and its journey (M08b); the greybox preparation path (G01 builds it first).

## Contract and design decisions
Round preparation flow (§4.4, DEFAULT): the director emits `PrepareRequested{preparationId, seed}` when Intermission starts, or from Lobby when the
host starts. Main hands the seed to the procgen worker, the renderer builds the map's meshes and uploads them, then main sends
`MapReady{preparationId, mapBytes}`; the sim validates the bytes and builds colliders; the director commits at the next Countdown and ignores a
stale `preparationId`. Track seeds = one session seed + the round index; a **reroll** draws the next seed (so a bug clip names the exact track)
and increments `PreparationId`, cancelling old work. Master §11.2a: the procgen worker produces data; the sim worker owns colliders; the main
thread owns GPU upload; keep the old presentation until the new one is usable; publish Ready only when generation, validation, colliders,
upload and shader warm-up are complete. If the conservative recipe also fails, show **Retry / Lobby** and keep the room and results; never load
an invalid map or reroll forever. Works with whatever biomes exist (the placeholder at first).
- **Dev map import (owner, 2026-10-03):** in test-enabled builds an authored `jj.map.v1` JSON (hand-made or edited) loads as the next round's
  map through the same validator (DEFAULT: `?test&map=<name>` loads `maps/<name>.json` from the build, or through the F05b surface), so a
  designed map can be imported later with dev work. No map export UI.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: M03, N07b, R03, S02. Provides: preparation to M08b, G01's loop (swaps in generated maps), F07 (seed in clips).

## Required tests
- Browser tests: a stale job never commits; failure shows Retry/Lobby; reroll replaces a prepared map; the 'reroll during preparation' journey edge variant.

## Evidence

title: P1-M09 · Sign kit
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-M09** (cites §8.1, §8.3; master §11.5a (signs)); master cut V2-50b part (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D4` · **Track:** `maps` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-R03. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
A data-driven Australian road-sign kit (family + text + pictogram as data, one code-drawn kit) that follows real sign grammar, including invented joke signs.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-procgen/src/signs/`, `web/host/src/render/signs/`, `assets/kit/signs/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Where biomes place signs (M04 places at least one direction and one warning sign).

## Contract and design decisions
Owner ruling 2026-10-02: new signs permitted within a faithful style. Source: <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_signs_in_Australia> (images on
Wikimedia Commons). Each sign follows a real family's **grammar**:
- **Warning:** yellow rotated-square diamond, black border and black legend or pictogram; short, upper-case, road-sign phrasing; the joke is in
  the wording, not a broken layout (e.g. "BLOODY BIG JUMPS AHEAD").
- **Direction/route:** green rectangle, white legend, route shield (e.g. A87 / STUART HWY), distances and arrows.
- **Tourist/information:** brown rectangle, white legend.
- Standard post mounting, sizing and placement (ahead of the hazard, at junctions); highway-style sans-serif lettering legible at the smallest tile.
- Pictograms from real symbol conventions (jump/crest, steep descent, unsealed road, animals).
New text and symbols are data (family + text + pictogram), rendered from one code-drawn kit: adding a sign never needs new geometry. Record
each sign's family and, for any real sign copied, its Commons source and licence in the asset sidecar. No new shapes or colour families
(the "incorrect signs" sheet shows the failure).

title: P1-M10 · Derby bowl arena with passive containment
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-M10** (cites master §11.4, §11.5a (rocks), §6.4; owner 2026-10-03); master cut V2-56 slice (owner 2026-10-03) (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D6` · **Track:** `maps` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-M01, P1-M05, P1-R03. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
One derby arena for the first derby: a seeded bowl with the rocks biome's look (red domes, quarry walls, boulders; R83 "derby is separate with
rocks vibes"), sized to the car count when the round is prepared, that keeps every car in by its shape alone. 0.1 learned this the hard way: cars
launched out of the bowl's sides until it got a vertical top wall and a flat lip, and an inverted flat→wall transition caught cars.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-procgen/src/arena/` (or `crates/jj-map` arena support + a small arena recipe), `assets/kit/arena/`, `web/host/src/render/kit/arena/`, `scenarios/derby/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Derby rules and scoring (P1-S10); the Overview camera (P1-R11); the round loop (P1-G06); other arena shapes (oval, figure-eight, quarry, island: later).

## Contract and design decisions
Owner direction 2026-10-03: the first derby is **passive containment** (the bowl's walls and lip keep cars in; **no shrinking
wall** or other arena-closing mechanism) and is **won on damage dealt** (R56: a 3-minute round ranked by raw damage points; late joiners are
allowed and simply have less time). A **last-man-standing** mode comes later (P1-S11, deferred) with a host switch for drop-in while playing.

- `jj.map.v1` gains an **arena** variant validated by `jj-map`: bounds, floor heightfield, containment wall profile, spawn-ring rule (any N:
  placement ghosts extra cars under spawn protection, as on tracks), optional centre mound/pillars and ramps; no route or gates.
- **Bowl shape:** one revolved profile from a smooth flat floor into a curved bank and a **vertical top wall with a flat lip** (no inverted
  concavity at the transition); the collider is the same profile as the mesh (trimesh or matching proxies). Rocks dressing (domes, boulders,
  quarry faces) from P1-M05's kit sits outside the playable bowl or as solid rammable features inside it.
- **Sized to the expected N** at preparation (arena radius grows with the car count so cars stay big in Overview, R22); mid-round joins never
  reshape terrain under cars (master §11.2a). Seeded and deterministic native/WASM, like the procgen core.
- **Passive containment only:** no shrinking wall, closing ring or damage zone.
- Validator: every navigable region reachable, no dead corners (bots can reach every region), no unintentional escapes.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: M01 map format, M05 rocks kit, R03 map renderer. Provides: the arena map to S10 (rules), R11 (Overview framing), G06 (round loop).

## Reuses / gap
Reuses the procgen core's seeding and M05's rocks kit, and 0.1's containment lessons (`git show v0.1-final:` the derby bowl and Coliseum fixes). Gap: no 0.2 arena.

## Required tests
- Scenario `bowl-containment`: cars rammed at the rim from many angles and speeds (including boosted and airborne) never leave the arena.
- Scenario `bowl-transition`: driving from floor to bank to wall never catches or launches a car at the transition.
- Arenas for 8, 16 and 32 cars validate and place every car; bytes identical native/WASM; a capture vs the rocks reference.

title: P1-N01 · `jj-types` + `jj-protocol` v1
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-N01** (cites §4.4, §5.1, §5.4); master cut V2-02 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D0` · **Track:** `net` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-F01. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
The shared vocabulary every other crate and the web apps speak: typed IDs and units, the controller state batch, the command enums, HUD
messages, signalling DTOs and the host worker ABI, all with golden byte vectors so the wire never drifts silently. On the critical path.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-types/`, `crates/jj-protocol/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Input shaping and scheduling (N06); seat logic (N07a); the server's use of the DTOs (N02/N03); TS bindings glue in `web/shared/` (N05).

## Contract and design decisions
Controller wire format v1 (plan §5.4, DEFAULT):
```text
StateBatch:  u8 type=0x10 | u8 minor | u16 batchSeq | u16 sentAtMs | u8 count      (7 bytes)
  record × count:
    u16 sourceHandle   (assigned by the host on claim; per connection)
    u16 sourceSeq      (wrapping, per source)
    i16 driveX, i16 driveY, i16 actionX, i16 actionY   (quantised −32767..32767)
    u8  flags          (bit0 available, bit1 driveTouch, bit2 actionTouch,
                        bit3 wheeliePreload, bit4 menuOpen)                  (13 bytes)
```
- One source = 20 bytes; 60 Hz = 1,200 B/s payload, under the 2,000 B/s target (R80). A batch splits when it would pass ~1,000 application
  bytes or 255 records, whichever first; extra batches go in the same flush, fairly rotated across sources; nothing is ever truncated.
- **Input age:** `sentAtMs` is the controller's monotonic clock (wrapping ms). The `cmd` channel carries `Ping{t}`/`Pong{t, hostT}` on connect
  and every 5 s; the host keeps a clock-offset estimate with ±RTT/2 uncertainty per endpoint. Receipts report sample-to-send,
  host-applied input age and action age as p50/p95/p99 with that uncertainty, never by comparing unsynchronised clocks.
- Axes carry the personal response curve already applied on the controller; game interpretation (DriveIntent, sectors, boost/drift) happens
  in `jj-input` on the host, the same path pads and keys use.
- **Cadence:** flush changing state up to 60 Hz; refresh unchanged state at 20 Hz; send neutral/cancel/unavailable immediately. The host
  neutralises a source after **250 ms** without fresh state and hands the car to autopilot after **2 s**.
- **Command channel:** `u8 version` + a `postcard`-encoded enum. Controller → host: `Hello{protocol, build, endpointId, resume?: endpointSecret}`,
  `Claim{requestId, name}`, `Action{actionId, sourceHandle, kind, roundId, lifeId, atSourceSeq}`, `Identify`, `SetName`, `SetCamera{fp|tp}`,
  `Ready{on}`, `Recover`, `SitOut`, `Leave`, `Menu{open}`, `Ping{t}`. Host → controller: `Welcome{seatId, number, colour, sourceHandle}`,
  `ClaimRejected{reason}`, `ActionResult{actionId, applied{tick}|expired|rejected{reason}}`, `RoomState{phase, you, countdown, results}`,
  `Pong{t, hostT}`, `Ended`. HUD updates (position, lap, boost, connection, pause reason) go on the **state** channel at ~10 Hz and on change.
  `Action.kind` = `wheelie{preloadMs}` | `utilityForward` | `utilityRear`. `RoomState.you` carries the seat's `roundId` and `lifeId`, which
  `Action`s echo. A `Hello` whose `protocol` differs gets `ClaimRejected{reason: build}`; the controller reloads once.
- **Discrete actions** (wheelie release, forward/rear utility) are detected on the controller by `jj-input` and sent as `Action` with a
  stable `actionId`. The host deduplicates, applies at a tick or returns `expired`/`rejected`; never executes an expired action late and never
  infers an edge from the lossy state stream (master §4.1).

Worker ABI (plan §4.4, DEFAULT; versioned in `jj-protocol`):
| Direction | Message | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| main → sim | `Init{abiVersion, rulesHash, mapBytes, vehicleSidecars, seed}` | canonical `jj.map.v1` bytes |
| main → sim | `NetBytes{endpointId, channel, bytes}` | raw controller bytes, forwarded as they arrive (no batching on main) |
| main → sim | `LocalSource{sourceId, axes, buttons, seq}` | host pads/keys, already sampled |
| main → sim | `Ui{commandId, command}` | host UI commands (start, End, reroll, camera…) |
| main → sim | `Lifecycle{visible, renderOk}` | composes pause reasons |
| main → sim | `MapReady{preparationId, mapBytes}` | a prepared round map, sent only after the renderer built and uploaded it; stale `preparationId` ignored |
| main → sim | `ReturnBuffer{buf}` | pooled snapshot buffer back to the worker |
| sim → main | `Snapshot{buf, tick, simTime, sessionRev}` | transferable; car transforms, wheel poses, part states/angles, debris transforms, HUD facts |
| sim → main | `Events{batch}` | ordered: joins, detaches, wrecks, laps, finishes, results, `PrepareRequested{preparationId, seed}` |
| sim → main | `Journal{bytes}` | applied-tick input journal chunks, kept on main for bug clips |
| sim → main | `Outbound{endpointId, channel, bytes}` | Welcome, ActionResult, HUD and room state for controllers |
Snapshots are bulk binary; if no pooled buffer is free the worker skips that publish, never blocks physics or drops events.

Also: signalling DTOs for §5.1 (room create/resolve/re-register, endpoint registration, signal messages `{from, to, kind, gen, payload}`,
ICE responses); quantisation helpers (`i16` −32767..32767, neutral/full-range/threshold preserved); wrapping sequence comparison for
`u16` seqs; the Ping/Pong clock-offset estimator with its ±RTT/2 uncertainty. `jj-types` has no I/O.

## Interfaces
- Provides: wire types to N02/N03/N05 (server + transport), N06 (input), N07a–c (session), S01/S02 (sim + worker), F05b
  (test messages), R01 (synthetic snapshot source implements the ABI), M01 (canonical-bytes conventions via postcard).

## Required tests
- Golden byte vectors for every message (committed files); round-trip property tests; fuzzed decoders (cargo-fuzz or proptest) never panic.
- Quantisation: neutral, full-range and threshold values survive.
- Batch splitting by the ~1,000-byte target and by >255 sources, with every record preserved.
- The Ping/Pong offset estimator recovers a known offset within its stated uncertainty.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Test output + golden files. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-N01/`.

## How this bead closes

## Working rules
Follow `AGENTS.md` (owner rules first) and `docs/process/bead-workflow.md`: check your own area, commit with `P1-N01` and the bead ID in the message, push, and close this bead once CI is green on a commit containing it (gate pass, ticked items, `receipt:<run url>`).

> Done only when the FELT, observable outcome above holds in the RUNNING game via the real host path. Passing unit/geometry tests is necessary but NOT sufficient.

title: P1-N02 · `jj-server` skeleton on Asupersync
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-N02** (cites §5.1, §5.2; R2); master cut V2-04 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D0` · **Track:** `net` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-F01, P1-F03. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
The Rust server's foundation on Asupersync (no Tokio, R2): base-path-aware static serving, `version`/`healthz`, and the SSE helper that
signalling rides on. It also qualifies Asupersync's server for long-lived streams (plan T4).

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-server/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Rooms and signalling (N03), ICE (N04), the image (D02).

## Contract and design decisions
- Static serving with base path (`/` or `/p/<id>/`); `GET B/assets/<hash>.<ext>` immutable long-cache with real 404s, never SPA HTML;
  `GET B/`, `B/host`, `B/c`, `B/j/<CODE>` serve the landing, host app, controller app and join link.
- `GET B/version` → `{build, protocol, realm}`; `GET B/healthz` liveness + readiness (TURN provider status reported, not fatal).
- SSE (plan §5.2): use `fetch()` with a streamed body and an SSE parser (not `EventSource`), so the bearer token goes in a header;
response `Content-Type: text/event-stream` (Cloudflare Tunnel streams only with this header); a comment heartbeat every **15 s**
(Cloudflare's proxy read timeout is ~100 s); event IDs monotonic per endpoint; reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`; the server keeps undelivered
messages for **60 s** (DEFAULT) per endpoint stream; buffers per endpoint grow with traffic and never cap endpoints; one SSE stream per
browser endpoint.
- Request size limits. `Cache-Control: no-store` on API responses. No Tokio in `cargo tree` (Asupersync 0.5.0 starting point,
  `default-features = false, features = ["native-runtime", "tls-webpki-roots"]`).

## Interfaces
- Consumes: F01, F03 pins. Provides: the server + SSE helper to N03/N04, the image to D02, the test server to F08/G00 journeys.

## Required tests
- Integration tests: serves a built web bundle under `/p/x/`; root-relative and unknown assets 404.
- A 5-minute SSE stream through a local proxy with heartbeats (log committed); slow readers don't block other streams.
- `cargo tree` no-Tokio check.

title: P1-N03 · Rooms and signalling
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-N03** (cites §5.1, §5.2); master cut V2-04 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D0` · **Track:** `net` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-N01, P1-N02, P1-N04. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Create/resolve rooms, register controller endpoints, relay WebRTC signalling over SSE, survive server restarts by host re-registration with a
stateless proof, report host liveness, and rate-limit abuse without ever capping players. The server never sees gameplay input (R77).

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-server/src/rooms/`, `crates/jj-server/src/signal/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
ICE credential minting (N04; N03 calls its provider in endpoint registration); the browser client (N05); host recovery after host death (deferred, R84).

## Contract and design decisions
Server API v1 (plan §5.1, DEFAULT). All paths under the deployment base path `B` (`/` in production, `/p/<id>/` in a preview).
JSON bodies, `Cache-Control: no-store` on API responses.
| Endpoint | Who | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET B/`, `B/host`, `B/c`, `B/j/<CODE>` | anyone | Landing, host app, controller app, join link (opens controller with the code) |
| `GET B/assets/<hash>.<ext>` | anyone | Immutable, long-cache static files; real 404s, never SPA HTML |
| `GET B/version` | anyone | `{build, protocol, realm}` |
| `GET B/healthz` | ops | Liveness + readiness (TURN provider status reported, not fatal) |
| `POST B/api/v1/rooms` | host | `{requestId, hostSecretHash}` → `201 {roomId, code, joinUrl, hostEndpointId, roomTicket, iceServers, iceExpiresAt}`; retry with the same `requestId` returns the same room; host endpoint registered as `hostEndpointId = "host"` |
| `PUT B/api/v1/rooms/<code>` | host | Re-register after a **server** restart: `{roomId, hostSecretHash, roomTicket}` + `Authorization: Bearer <hostSecret>` → `200 {code, roomTicket}`; if another room took the code meanwhile, a fresh code + ticket for the same `roomId` |
| `GET B/api/v1/rooms/<code>` | anyone | `{status: available\|host-unreachable\|ended\|not-found, roomId, build, realm}` |
| `POST B/api/v1/rooms/<roomId>/endpoints` | controller | `{requestId, endpointId, endpointSecretHash}` → `201 {iceServers, iceExpiresAt}`; registers a signalling endpoint (not a seat) and returns the initial ICE list in the same round trip |
| `GET B/api/v1/rooms/<roomId>/signal?endpoint=<id>` | both | SSE stream |
| `POST B/api/v1/rooms/<roomId>/signal` | both | `{from, to, kind: offer\|answer\|candidate\|restart\|bye, gen, payload}` |
| `POST B/api/v1/ice` | both | `{roomId, endpointId}` → `{iceServers, expiresAt}` refresh of the initial list (STUN + coturn); bearer = that endpoint's secret |
| `POST B/api/v1/ice/fallback` | both | `{roomId, endpointId, reason}` → Cloudflare TURN entries, or `429 {retryAfterMs}`, or `503 {reason: relay-unavailable}` |
| `POST B/api/v1/rooms/<roomId>/end` | host | Ends the room; a tombstone stops stale re-registration |
Authentication: every non-public call carries `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`; the server stores only SHA-256 hashes; secrets are
128-bit random, base64url. Never log secrets or full join URLs with secrets.

- **Room codes:** 4 characters from `ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789` (no O/0/I/1/L), case-insensitive entry, a small deny-list of rude
  words, random with collision retry. A code is a locator, never a credential.
- **State:** rooms live in memory. A server restart drops them; hosts re-register (`PUT`) on their next SSE reconnect and keep their codes;
  controllers re-register their endpoints (the same idempotent `POST …/endpoints` with their existing id and secret hash), so later ICE
  restarts can still signal; existing WebRTC connections keep working. Restart signal = `404 {reason: unknown-room}` on the SSE `GET` or a
  signalling `POST`; the host answers with `PUT`; a controller retries registration with backoff (0.5 s doubling to 5 s).
- **Re-registration proof:** `roomTicket = base64url(HMAC-SHA256(JJ_ROOM_KEY, realm‖roomId‖code‖hostSecretHash))`; `JJ_ROOM_KEY` is a
  per-deployment secret that survives restarts (deploy secrets; a fixed dev key locally). A `PUT` whose ticket doesn't verify gets `403`.
  Stateless check, **not** the deferred registration CAS (R84).
- **Endpoint conflicts:** an `endpointId` already registered with a different secret hash gets `409`; the controller generates a new endpoint.
- **Room liveness** (DEFAULT, TUNE): the host's SSE stream is its heartbeat. 30 s without it → `GET rooms/<code>` reports `host-unreachable`;
  10 minutes without it → the room record is dropped. A host that comes back re-registers with its ticket. `End` leaves a compact tombstone
  (kept 24 h, in memory) so an ended room is never re-registered. Lifetimes, not counts: nothing limits how many rooms or endpoints exist.
- **Abuse limits** (DEFAULT; rates, never player caps, R66): token buckets per client IP (the tunnel's `CF-Connecting-IP`) on room creation
  (burst 10, then 1 per 10 s) and endpoint registration (burst 64, then 4 per s); signalling `POST`s per endpoint (burst 64, then 20 per s).
  A limited call gets `429 {retryAfterMs}`, clients retry. A party of any size behind one IP joins within seconds.

SSE (plan §5.2): use `fetch()` with a streamed body and an SSE parser (not `EventSource`), so the bearer token goes in a header;
response `Content-Type: text/event-stream` (Cloudflare Tunnel streams only with this header); a comment heartbeat every **15 s**
(Cloudflare's proxy read timeout is ~100 s); event IDs monotonic per endpoint; reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`; the server keeps undelivered
messages for **60 s** (DEFAULT) per endpoint stream; buffers per endpoint grow with traffic and never cap endpoints; one SSE stream per
browser endpoint.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: N01 DTOs, N02 server/SSE, N04's provider (initial ICE list in the create and endpoint-registration responses).
- Provides: the room/signalling API to N05 (client), G00 (hello room), C03 (controller states from `GET rooms/<code>`), G03/JN7 (restart).

## Required tests
Integration tests (virtual time where timers matter):
- create → resolve → register endpoint (ICE servers in the response) → offer/answer/candidates over SSE;

title: P1-N04b · Cloudflare TURN lazy fallback issuance (R92)
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-N04b** (cites §5.3 (Cloudflare TURN is lazy, One credential broker, Issuance limits)); master cut new, R88, R92 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D5` · **Track:** `net` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`, `ev:hardware`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-N04, P1-N05. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Status notes
**Already done outside the tracker (2026-10-02):** the spend guard (`tools/turn-guard/guard.py`, TrueNAS app `jammers-turn-guard`: 5-min
GraphQL polling, push alert at 10 % of the free 1,000 GB, deletes every `jammers-` key at 25 % or at 2 GB/hour on one tag, alarm when blind
15 min, dry-run mode), Cloudflare budget emails ($1/$10) and the key `jammers-fallback` (secret in `~/.config/jammers/cf-turn-key.env`).
Measured: deleting the key, revoking a credential or letting its TTL lapse does **not** stop an issued credential (one minted with a 2-minute
TTL was still allocating ~1 h 50 min later). So the remaining control is issuance itself, which this bead builds. **No Cloudflare
credential is issued anywhere until this bead passes.**

## Purpose and observable outcome
Build the only path that issues Cloudflare TURN credentials: lazy, authenticated, idempotent, rate-limited (never capped), through one
`turn-broker` that alone holds the Cloudflare token, plus the client-side trigger rules and the "Finding a relay…" state.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-server/src/ice/` (fallback client + `turn-broker` role), `web/shared/transport/` (fallback trigger), `jammers-deploy` (broker deployment, its secret, per-backend secrets).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The spend guard (done). The initial ICE list (N04). Controller-state wording beyond "Finding a relay…"/"No route" (C03).

## Contract and design decisions
Cloudflare TURN is lazy (R92, plan §5.3):
- Never in the initial list (an issued Cloudflare credential can't be revoked: measured, it outlives key deletion, revocation and its TTL).
- Either side calls `POST /ice/fallback` only when, for that peer connection: ICE reaches `failed`; or gathering finished with no coturn
  `relay` candidate and the connection isn't `connected` 3 s later; or it still isn't `connected` 8 s after the offer (TUNE). It then merges
  the Cloudflare entries with `setConfiguration()` and restarts ICE (gen + 1). Keep the returned URLs (UDP, TCP, TLS on their documented
  ports) except any on port 53; the TLS-on-443 entry is the one UDP-blocked networks need.
- Credentials carry `customIdentifier = jj-<realm>-<roomId>-<endpointId>` and a 30 min TTL, re-requested only while the peer still needs a
  relay. A credential belongs to an **endpoint**: the host (one endpoint, many peers) reuses one fallback credential for every peer.
- **One credential broker:** a single `turn-broker` (a role of the `jj-server` binary, deployed once from `jammers-deploy`) holds the only
  copy of the Cloudflare API token and enforces the limits; backends call it on the internal network with a per-backend secret
  `HMAC-SHA256(brokerKey, previewId)` (injected by the publish workflow, recomputed by the broker) and forward the client IP taken only
  from the tunnel's `CF-Connecting-IP`. Each request carries a `requestId`: a retried lost response returns the same credential.
- **Issuance limits are rates, not totals:** token buckets per endpoint (burst 2, then 1 per 5 min), per room (burst 32, then 1 per 2 s), per
  client IP (burst 32, then 1 per 5 s). Worst case: 40 guests behind one IP on a UDP-blocked network get 32 credentials at once and the other
  8 within 40 s. A refused call returns `429 {retryAfterMs}`; the controller shows "Finding a relay…" and retries. Abuse limits, never player
  caps; the guard's egress thresholds bound the cost (TUNE).
- A provider failure drops only that provider's entries and shows "relay unavailable" when none is left; direct paths keep working.
- Playtest topology risk: the host laptop sits on `192.168.10.0/24`, coturn on TrueNAS `192.168.11.12`, exposed WAN-side to AU sources
  only; a cellular guest probably can't reach a LAN host through coturn and falls back to Cloudflare. Observe it (Q02 checklist; Q-N1).

## Interfaces
- Consumes: N04's provider trait fallback slot; N05's no-op relay-fallback hook (this bead implements it).
- Provides: `/ice/fallback` to both sides; the "Finding a relay…"/"relay unavailable" signals C03 shows; the live Cloudflare path N08 measures.

## Required tests
Mocked Cloudflare API + virtual time:
- trigger rules fire only in the three §5.3 cases;
- 40 endpoints behind one IP all get credentials within the stated worst case and none is refused permanently;
- a retried `requestId` returns the same credential; two backends share one bucket (via the broker);
- with the key unset the room keeps working on direct/coturn paths and shows "relay unavailable".
One controlled live run (`ev:hardware`): `iceTransportPolicy: "relay"` with coturn unreachable → fallback → connects through Cloudflare,
once restricted to the TLS-443 entry; the issued tag appears in the guard's per-tag listing; the guard's dry-run against a synthetic breach
still alerts and would delete the key.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Test log; the live run's redacted stats and URLs; guard dry-run output. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-N04b/`.

Follow `AGENTS.md` (owner rules first) and `docs/process/bead-workflow.md`: check your own area, commit with `P1-N04b` and the bead ID in the message, push, and close this bead once CI is green on a commit containing it (gate pass, ticked items, `receipt:<run url>`).

title: P1-N05 · Browser WebRTC transport and signalling client (shared)
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-N05** (cites §5.2, §5.3); master cut V2-05 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D0` · **Track:** `net` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-N01, P1-N03, P1-N04. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
The one transport library both the host and the controller use: fetch-streamed SSE signalling with reconnect, the controller-offerer flow,
pre-negotiated channels, generations, ICE restart then rebuild, credential refresh, server-restart re-registration and selected-path stats.

## Scope (owned paths)
`web/shared/transport/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The fallback issuance and trigger (N04b fills the no-op hook); controller UI states (C03); the input codec (N06).

## Contract and design decisions
SSE (plan §5.2): use `fetch()` with a streamed body and an SSE parser (not `EventSource`), so the bearer token goes in a header;
response `Content-Type: text/event-stream` (Cloudflare Tunnel streams only with this header); a comment heartbeat every **15 s**
(Cloudflare's proxy read timeout is ~100 s); event IDs monotonic per endpoint; reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`; the server keeps undelivered
messages for **60 s** (DEFAULT) per endpoint stream; buffers per endpoint grow with traffic and never cap endpoints; one SSE stream per
browser endpoint.

WebRTC (plan §5.3):
- **Controller is the offerer.** Resolve the code (`GET rooms/<code>`), register its endpoint (response carries the initial ICE list), open
  its SSE stream, then offer at once. Direct negotiation never waits for a relay fallback.
- `RTCPeerConnection({iceServers, iceTransportPolicy: "all"})`, trickle ICE, no candidate stripping, mDNS host candidates allowed (R79).
  Test browsers launch with `--disable-features=WebRtcHideLocalIpsWithMdns` (test-only).
- **Secure contexts:** `crypto.subtle`, wake lock and camera need HTTPS or `localhost`. Previews are HTTPS; dev loads from `localhost`; a
  cross-machine plain-HTTP test browser uses `--unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure=<origin>` (test-only). Real phones use previews.
- Two **pre-negotiated** data channels (`negotiated: true`): id 0 `state` (`ordered: false, maxRetransmits: 0`), id 1 `cmd` (reliable, ordered).
- Negotiation generation `gen` tags every offer/answer/candidate; the host fences older gens.
- Recovery: on `disconnected` for 3 s, or on page resume, the controller tries `restartIce()` with a new offer (gen + 1); if still not
  connected after 5 s it builds a new peer connection (gen + 1). Same seat throughout.
- **Initial ICE list (R88):** Cloudflare STUN `stun:stun.cloudflare.com:3478` + coturn `turn:turn.dilger.dev:3479?transport=udp` (UDP only,
  AU sources only; `docs/infra/turn-and-previews.md`). coturn credentials minted by `jj-server` with the TURN REST scheme:
  `username = "<expiry>:<endpointId>"`, `credential = base64(HMAC-SHA1(secret, username))`, TTL 7,200 s (DEFAULT); refresh at 75 % of the TTL
  via `POST /ice` and `setConfiguration()`.
- Diagnostics: both ends read the selected candidate pair (`local/remote candidateType`, `relayProtocol`) and RTT; redact IPs.
- The host holds one peer connection per controller endpoint; report any browser ceiling honestly, never impose our own (R66).

Also: the host's re-register `PUT` after a server restart (on `404 {reason: unknown-room}`); the controller's endpoint re-registration with
backoff (0.5 s doubling to 5 s); ICE refresh via `setConfiguration`; a **no-op relay-fallback hook** that P1-N04b implements;
selected-path stats (host / srflx / coturn relay / Cloudflare relay + its transport) exposed for diagnostics (G00, R07) and receipts (N08).

## Interfaces
- Consumes: N01 DTOs, N03 API, N04 ICE list.
- Provides: transport to G00 (hello room), C02/C03 (controller), the host app, N04b (hook), N08 (stats), R07 (diagnostics overlay).

## Required tests
Playwright (two contexts, loopback, mDNS test flag):
- connect over loopback; forced `relay` policy through a local coturn container with N04 credentials;
- kill the connection → restart → the same endpoint reconnects at gen + 1 without re-registering; stale-generation candidates ignored;
- restart `jj-server` mid-session → data channel stays up and the host re-registers its code.

title: P1-N06 · `jj-input` + controller WASM
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-N06** (cites §5.4, §7.3, §7.6; master §4.1–§4.4); master cut V2-10, V2-05 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D0` · **Track:** `net` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-N01. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
One input-interpretation crate shared by controllers (as a small WASM) and the host worker: shaping, DriveIntent, sector detection with
hysteresis, wheelie preload/release, action IDs, freshness and the send scheduler, so touch, pads and keys mean the same thing (plan T5).

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-input/`, `crates/jj-wasm-input/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Controller UI (C02), host pads/keys sampling (C05), the vehicle response to DriveIntent (S03), utilities' effects (S08).

## Contract and design decisions
- Response curves and dead zones (the personal curve is applied on the controller; the game interpretation on the host).
- **DriveIntent** (steer/throttle/brake/reverse): DRIVE X steers; up throttles; down brakes, then reverses near rest; axes shaped
  independently so diagonal steering doesn't reduce full throttle; full brake is reachable before the wheelie detent.
- **Sector detection** for ACTION with hysteresis and a neutral re-arm: up = forward utility, down = rear utility, right = boost (held),
  left = handbrake drift (held). Discrete utilities fire on intentional sector entry.
- **Wheelie** (plan §7.3): DRIVE pulled past the full-brake point (y < −0.85) preloads; a **release** = the stick leaves the preload zone
  and passes y > −0.3 within 250 ms (easing off slowly is just braking); lift scales with preload time (max at 0.4 s); holding past 1.2 s
  (TUNE) cancels the preload. Sent as `Action{kind: wheelie{preloadMs}}` so a later neutral sample can't erase it.
- Stable **action IDs**; pointer cancel, visibility loss, device disconnect and pause neutralise and never fire a wheelie or utility.
- Freshness state per source; the **send scheduler** (§5.4 cadence: flush changing state up to 60 Hz, refresh unchanged state at 20 Hz,
  prompt neutral/cancel/unavailable; changed-state sends satisfy the refresh deadline: no second 20 Hz stream on top); batching per §5.4.
- `jj-wasm-input` exposes this + `jj-protocol` encoding to controllers; **≤ 150 KB gzipped** (DEFAULT).

## Interfaces
- Consumes: N01 wire types. Provides: input semantics to C02 (controller), C05 (host pads/keys), S02 (worker interprets NetBytes/LocalSource), S08, C06 (prompt detection).

## Required tests
Property tests (proptest): diagonal steer doesn't reduce full throttle; brake reaches full before the wheelie detent; pointer cancel never
fires a wheelie or utility; a press+release between two sends still yields one action; refresh never stacks on change sends. A bundle-size
check of the WASM build.

title: P1-N07a · Session: seats, claims, resume, Identify
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-N07a** (cites §5.5, §9; master §4.4, §5); master cut V2-03 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D1` · **Track:** `net` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-N01. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
The host's seat reducer: idempotent claims, resume by secret hash, duplicate-tab fencing, stable per-seat number and colour for any N,
Identify with a rate limit, and Leave/Sit out at tick boundaries. "One car per seat, no phantom seats" is the 0.1 lesson re-expressed.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-session/src/seats/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The round director (N07b), results (N07c), the controller's join UI (C03), autopilot driving (S07).

## Contract and design decisions
- Opening a URL never claims a seat. `Claim{requestId, name}` → `Welcome{seatId, number, colour, sourceHandle}`; retries with the same
  `requestId` can't create a second car.
- Controller endpoints keep `endpointId` + `endpointSecret` in `localStorage`, namespaced by realm (production vs preview id) **and room**
  (master §16.2a); each room gets a fresh endpoint. Reconnect sends `Hello{resume: endpointSecret}`; the host matches the stored hash and
  returns the **same seat, car, progress and score**. A duplicate tab with the same secret fences the older one ("Playing in another tab").
- Explicit device handoff is deferred (R84): a new device gets a new seat.
- Per-seat number and colour with **no cap**: colours from a curated palette reused with distinct numbers as N grows; numbers are stable
  increasing display labels, not capped at 99.
- **Identify** with a 3 s rate limit per seat (master §5.2); auto-fires on join and respawn.
- **Leave / Sit out** at tick boundaries: car withdrawn with a visible cue; debris stays; standings kept (master §4.4).
- Names (plan §9): ≤ 32 graphemes, text only, NFC, trimmed; blank reverts to the default; case-folded duplicates gain the seat-number suffix (master §10.6).
- Re-express the 0.1 cases (§14): `server/room_seats.py`, `static/js/engine/roomSeatRegistry.js`, `tests/integration/host-authority.test.js`,
  `room-seat-registry.test.js`, `server/test_seat_input_safety.py` (read with `git show v0.1-final:<path>`): one car per seat; stale input
  neutralised; retries don't duplicate seats. Nothing is ported as code.

## Interfaces
- Provides: seat state to S02 (worker), F05a (seats as JSON), C03 (Welcome/fencing), C05 (claim-by-press), R06 (Identify), N07b.

## Required tests
Property tests over random join/leave/resume/duplicate-tab/claim-retry sequences: one car per seat, no phantom seats, numbers stable, N up
to large generated values with no truncation; reducer boundary tables for Leave/Sit out timing and the Identify rate limit.

## Acceptance

## Evidence

title: P1-N07b · Session: round director
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-N07b** (cites §9, §4.4; master §10.6, §10.8); master cut V2-100, V2-79b (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D2` · **Track:** `net` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-N07a. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
The host-owned RoundDirector that runs the party by itself: Lobby → Preparing → Countdown → Running → Finalising → Intermission →
Countdown…, Ready/force-start, cohort freeze, presentation-clock timers, auto-next, End/Disband, pause composition and preparation IDs.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-session/src/director/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Results/standings (N07c); the browser wiring and journeys (G01); map preparation (G01 with the greybox, M08a with procgen).

## Contract and design decisions
- **Phases:** Lobby → Preparing → Countdown → Running → Finalising → Intermission → Countdown … (master §10.8). The next track prepares in the
  background during Intermission (`PrepareRequested` emitted when Intermission starts, or from Lobby when the host starts); if it isn't ready
  when Intermission ends, a visible Preparing phase waits for it or its conservative fallback. End returns to Lobby; Disband ends the room.
- **Lobby warm-up** (§9): claimed seats free-drive on the greybox with collisions/damage on, no progress/lap/score.
- **Start policy:** start when all active human seats are Ready (source-fresh, non-parked humans; nonempty), or host **Start now** with a
  **10 s warning** to not-ready controllers (banner + vibration where supported), then everyone plays with their current car (R31). Start now
  again skips the countdown.
- **Countdown cohort freeze:** freeze the start cohort when countdown begins; new seats join with current selection and don't restart it;
  an original seat un-readying cancels a ready-based countdown; force-start overrides Ready only, never asset/physics readiness.
- **Intermission:** ~60 s on the presentation clock (results + reel), skippable by the host, then auto-start (R38, R50); new players join
  during intermission and are seated for the next round; no driving during Intermission.
- **Pause composition:** `manual`, `host-hidden`, `renderer-unavailable`, `performance-stall`, `fault`; manual/hidden/fault pauses freeze
  countdown and intermission time. Controller loss never pauses (R45).
- **Preparation IDs:** each reroll increments `PreparationId`; stale map jobs can't commit; End cancels pending jobs and voids any unfinished round.
- With no active human seats, settle in Lobby; never start a zero-player auto-round loop.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: N07a seats. Provides: the director to N07c, G01 (browser wiring), M08a (preparation), R07 (phase UI), A03 (moment events).

## Required tests
Reducer tests for the master §10.8 boundary table: join during countdown, unready during countdown, End during preparation, reroll during
preparation, pause during intermission; plus force-start warning timing and the no-zero-player rule.

## Acceptance

## Evidence

title: P1-N07c · Session: results and standings
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-N07c** (cites §7.5, §9; master §10.12); master cut V2-78, V2-102 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D2` · **Track:** `net` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-N07b. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Race classification and the session standings shown at results: finishers, DNF/DNS, ties, the championship points table with no
truncated tail, the finish bonus, committed exactly once per round, in memory only (R84).

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-session/src/results/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Race progress and finish detection (S05); the results screen (R07).

## Contract and design decisions
Master §10.12 Race rules (engineering defaults, versioned ruleset):
- Finish ordering by authoritative tick plus interpolated checkpoint crossing fraction; an exact tie shares place/points (stable seat order
  only for display). Unfinished entrants rank after finishers by legal unwrapped progress, then by the tick that progress was reached;
  equal values share place.
- Withdrawn at finalisation → frozen progress, **DNF**, never a finish bonus; returning before finalisation resumes the same result record. A
  finished seat can't Leave/return to become unfinished. Seats that never entered → **DNS**, zero.
- **Championship conversion:** ranks 1–10 get `[25,18,15,12,10,8,6,4,2,1]`; every later classified rank gets 1 (no truncated array). A Race
  finisher earns **+5** (host-configurable next round); DNF earns its placement points only. Tied entrants receive the points of their shared
  competition rank (1,1,3, not 1,1,2).
- Late joiners are classified from where they actually finish (inherited progress is not a completed timed lap).
- `CommitResult` idempotent by `RoundId`; rejects a conflicting payload for an already committed round. In-memory session standings only
  (nothing persists across host death, R84).

## Interfaces
- Consumes: N07b director events; S05 progress/finish facts. Provides: standings to R07 (results), G01 (JN3), A03 (winner cue), the controller `RoomState.results`.

## Required tests
- Fixture tests: simultaneous finishes, ties, late joiners, leave/return, all-stuck deadline, repeated commit.

title: P1-N08 · Network qualification harness and receipts
description:

**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-N04b, P1-N05, P1-G00. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Measured, honest receipts for every connection path the playtest might use (direct LAN, coturn, Cloudflare TLS-443, loss/jitter), with
input age and bytes, so the playtest's network behaviour is a known quantity. Real phones on cellular and client-isolated Wi-Fi are
P1-Q02 checklist rows (and answer Q-N1).

## Scope (owned paths)
`web/tests/net/`, `docs/evidence/P1-N08/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The unplugged-pad row (P1-C05). Real-device rows (P1-Q02).

## Contract and design decisions
Master §13.3a qualification list. Measure: sample-to-send (controller), host-applied input age (p50/p95/p99 with the Ping/Pong ±RTT/2
uncertainty, §5.4), action age, payload and wire bytes (label counter layers; browser stats don't expose everything), selected candidate
pair. Scripted loss/jitter with `tc netem` on a test interface on eris. Redact IPs/SDP/credentials. Never equate application bytes with billed
relay usage. A direct path is not proof of LAN locality; claim LAN from the controlled test topology.
Paths:
- controller on eris → host on the Mac over the real home Wi-Fi (direct; eris's browser loads the Mac's page with the §5.3 secure-context
  test flag `--unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure=<origin>`);
- the same pair forced through the **real coturn** (test-only ICE override to its LAN address, since the WAN VIP is WAN-side only; if the
  FortiGate doesn't route the home LAN to `192.168.11.12`, record that instead);
- forced through a **local coturn container**;
- the **Cloudflare fallback over TLS 443** (the one live N04b run);
- scripted loss/jitter with `tc netem` on eris;
- 60 Hz changing input ≤ **2,000 B/s payload per source**.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: N04b, N05 stats, the G00 hello room. Provides: receipts to Q02 and the Q-N1 decision (O9).

## Required tests
- The automated receipt runs listed above, each producing a receipt file.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
The receipts (`ev:hardware`). Phones on cellular → the home-LAN host and client-isolated Wi-Fi are P1-Q02 rows and answer Q-N1. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-N08/`.

title: P1-R01 · Renderer foundation and backend decision
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-R01** (cites §4.3, §6.1, §10, §15.2); master cut V2-23 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).

## Purpose and observable outcome
Stand up the host renderer and decide its backend with numbers: port Spike J's 24×24 bench into the host app, measure WebGPURenderer (WebGPU
and its WebGL2 backend) vs WebGLRenderer headed on the Mac's GPU, and own the host capability check so a host that can't run explains why
instead of opening a broken room. Rendering work starts before the sim worker exists by driving it from a synthetic snapshot source.

## Scope (owned paths)
`web/host/src/render/` (foundation, backend selection, synthetic snapshot source, capability check).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Instanced vehicles (R02), map rendering (R03), grid layout (R04), cameras (R05), the in-world look (R10).

## Contract and design decisions
- Measure in **headed** browsers on the Mac (M1 Pro, the reference host that drives the TCL), and on triton's GTX 1080 or eris's RTX 2080
  SUPER as extra data points when their GPUs are clear (eris's GPU is shared with audio jobs, so check first); label the machine; never
  headless/SwiftShader numbers.
- DEFAULT rule: pick **WebGPURenderer** if it is within 15 % of WebGLRenderer and instancing + per-tile viewports work; otherwise
  **WebGLRenderer** for Playtest 1 and record why. A forced fallback path renders the same frame.
- **Host capability check** (§10, R01): before creating a room, check WebGL2 or WebGPU, WASM and module workers. If one is missing, explain why
  and offer **Join** or another device instead of opening a room it can't run (experience direction §3; master J01).
- Interpolated scene updates from snapshots, driven at first by a **synthetic snapshot source** implementing the §4.4 ABI (`Snapshot{buf,
  tick, simTime, sessionRev}`); P1-S02 swaps in the real worker. Interpolation pairs never cross a respawn.
- three r186+ stable, bundled (no CDN).

## Interfaces
- Consumes: F03 pins, N01 ABI types. Provides: renderer + synthetic source to R02, R03, R04, R09; capability check to the host landing flow (G00/C01).

## Reuses / gap
Reuses Spike J's 24×24 bench (J `REPORT.md`). Gap: no host app renderer, no backend decision.

## Required tests
- Bench table (headed Playwright on the real GPU) per backend at 1080p and 4K; forced-fallback capture equality.
- Playwright: a browser with WebGL2 and WebGPU disabled gets the capability explanation and a Join link, and no room is created.

title: P1-R02 · Instanced vehicle renderer
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-R02** (cites §6.1, §6.3, §10); master cut V2-23 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D1` · **Track:** `render` · **Machine:** `on:mac` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:hardware`, `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-R01, P1-V02. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Render every car, loose part and detached part with **one InstancedMesh per part type** so draw calls per tile stay constant in N (216 draws
for 24 cars × 24 tiles vs 3,602 naive), with per-tile LOD classes sharing one instance buffer, paint from the identity colour, and buffers
that grow without a cap.

## Scope (owned paths)
`web/host/src/render/vehicles/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Map rendering (R03), cameras (R05), identity overlays (R06), the in-world look materials (R10).

## Contract and design decisions
§6.1 rows adopted as REQUIRED/DEFAULT:
- **One InstancedMesh per part type** across all cars (REQUIRED). Reference row (Spike J `REPORT.md`): 24×24, 1080p, LOD1, instanced, culling
  off → **216 draws, 506 k tris, 3.6 ms median / 5.1 ms p90** on an M1 Pro (5.1 / 6.4 ms at 4K).
- **Paint key** (REQUIRED identity colour path): atlas texels that are pure white tint by `instanceColor`; glass/lamps/livery keep colour; one
  material for all cars.
- **LOD per tile** (DEFAULT): all cars in a tile share a LOD class (tile height ≥ 540 px LOD0, ≥ 200 px LOD1, else LOD2). One InstancedMesh per
  part type **per LOD class**, all sharing one instance-matrix/colour buffer per part type; each tile's render pass shows only its LOD class's
  meshes, so heterogeneous tiles cost no extra uploads.
- Shadow map once per frame, not per tile. Instancing per part type, not BatchedMesh (BatchedMesh flat draws hold only for one shared camera
  and conflict with per-part detach).
- Loose parts = the part's instance with the hinge rotation applied; detached parts = the same part-type instance with a physics-driven
  matrix; a missing part shows the core's dark bay; detached parts keep the owner's paint colour.
- **Growable instance buffers, no cap** (R66). Perf receipts report draws, tris and frame time.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: R01 renderer + synthetic snapshots, V02 GLB/sidecar. Provides: car rendering to R05, R06, R09, R10, S04c (capture strip), V03 (damage strip, LOD ladder), M02, G04.

## Reuses / gap
Reuses Spike J's instancing bench as the named reference row; gap: production renderer with LOD-per-tile and damage instances.

## Required tests
- Headed Mac bench at the §6.1 reference row (`ev:hardware`).
- Captures: a car with loose and detached parts (angles from the synthetic snapshot source) in adjacent tiles at different LOD classes.
- A test that instance buffers grow past their initial size without a cap.

In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence

description:

## Purpose and observable outcome
Render `jj.map.v1` maps (terrain, road surfaces, barriers, dressing kit pieces, props) and build the renderer side of the kit-piece
registry: one code-built geometry module per registry id, instanced where repeated, so biomes add pieces by adding data + a module.

## Scope (owned paths)
`web/host/src/render/map/`, `web/host/src/render/kit/generic/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The registry schema and generic entries (M01 owns the data); biome kit pieces (M04–M07); signs (M09); the in-world graphics (R10).

## Contract and design decisions
- Terrain heightfield, road surfaces with **distinguishable surface IDs** (tarmac, packed dirt, gravel, rock, off-track), barriers, dressing
  kit pieces and props from `jj.map.v1` (§8.1; units: mm positions, cm heights).
- **Kit-piece registry** (§8.1): versioned data per piece (id, parameter schema, collider proxy, LOD rule) in `assets/kit/<family>/*.json`,
  validated by `jj-map`. R03 builds one code-built geometry module per registry id; repeated pieces are instanced; draws scale with kit-piece
  **types**, not instances. The greybox uses the generic pieces (barrier, post, box building, cone, bin).

  for the render track).

description:

## Purpose and observable outcome
The pure layout function behind the TV: `layout(displayRect, safeArea, seats) → tiles` for any N and any aspect, seat order kept, never black,
reflowing (animated) only on join/leave, implementing the layout rule and gap treatment the owner accepted at G-DESIGN.

## Scope (owned paths)
`web/host/src/layout/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Cameras per tile (R05), HUD in tiles (R07), any-aspect profiles (R08).

## Contract and design decisions
- Pure function `layout(displayRect, safeArea, seats) → tiles`, any aspect; seat order (join order, never race position); animated reflow
  (~300 ms, duration from tokens/U05) on join/leave only; spare cells show QR/"join now"/standings, never black; one player fills the screen
  with a corner QR. Never truncates the list (no cap).
- The rule is **U02's accepted pseudocode** (§3a: balanced rows first; last row centred with wider tiles within the aspect band; leftover cells
  show QR + standings), replacing master §6.2's filler default if the owner picked another.
- Master §6.2 starting constraints: rows·cols ≥ N minimising unused area; tile aspect in a playable band (~1.2–2.0 TP, FP a little narrower);
  portrait stacks vertically; ultrawide adds columns; N = 2 evaluates horizontal and vertical splits.
Built to the accepted POC set (`art/ui/accepted/<date>/`, P1-U04); captures are judged against the matching accepted screen by a fresh-eyes review note (§13b.4: images opened at gameplay size, named reference, elements present/absent/ambiguous, first-look reading, defects, before/after per repair). description:

## Purpose and observable outcome
Everything the TV shows around the 3D: the per-tile HUD, the lobby (QR + code + player strip over the warm-up), results and intermission,
the host's controls and the diagnostics overlay, built to the accepted POC TV mocks.

## Scope (owned paths)

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The reel (R09), any-aspect profiles (R08), the round wiring (G01), audio captions (A03 places them per the mocks).

## Contract and design decisions
- **Lobby** (§9): big QR + code always visible in lobby/intermission (QR rule from U01: plain, full quiet zone, nothing in the middle; QR
  encoder bundled, R70), the player strip (number, name, colour, Ready, connection), over the warm-up; lobby at any N (compact cards → chips,
  never "max players").
- **HUD per tile** (§10): position, lap, boost meter, wreck/respawn countdown, connection state (autopilot, reconnecting).

## Purpose and observable outcome
The derby's shared screen: one Overview camera framing every car big and readable on the TV, with identity rings and edge-band HUD, and a
host switch between Grid and Overview at any time. The POC already designs it (U02/U05); this builds it.

`web/host/src/camera/overview/`, `web/host/src/ui/overview/`.

## Contract and design decisions
Overview camera (master §6.4, R22, R23): one camera framing the action, no split. Frames the **cars' bounding box** plus margin
(never empty arena), clamped to arena bounds, fixed pitch ≈ 55–65°, never rotates, critically damped zoom; at high N it settles at "whole arena" and
stays (stability beats tightness). Every human-controlled car stays visible; never crop an outlier to hit a median-size target (a hard spread gives
a non-blocking Grid suggestion). Identity: nameplate + number + colour ring under each car, scaled by camera distance (nameplate ≥ 28 px at 4K).
HUD in thin edge bands (the 3-minute timer, damage-points standings). Host can switch Grid ⇄ Overview **at any time, including mid-round**, with

title: P1-S01 · `jj-sim` core and scenario runner
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S01** (cites §6.1, §7.1, §7.2, §8.1, §14); master cut V2-06, V2-07 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D1` · **Track:** `sim` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-N01, P1-M01. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
The authoritative simulation core (R61): a Rapier world built from `jj.map.v1`, a raycast vehicle, seeded RNG, a full-state hash, an
applied-tick input journal and a bootstrap scenario runner, plus a Rapier 0.36 API fixture that pins the semantics every later sim bead
relies on. On the critical path (… M01 → S01 → S02 …).

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/`, `crates/jj-tools/src/scenario/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The browser worker (S02), feel tuning (S03), damage (S04*), race rules (S05), placement (S06), autopilot (S07), utilities (S08); the shared introspection surface and `jj sim` (F05a turns S01's runner into it; S01 doesn't depend on F05a).

## Contract and design decisions
Time and ticks (plan §7.1): 120 Hz fixed step, `dt = 1/120` (R61). The worker owns the accumulator and steps whole ticks; rendering
interpolates between the last two snapshots. **Tick order:** apply commands and inputs due at this tick → set vehicle controls and surface
friction → `update_vehicle` against current query data → `step` → read contact data and build damage episodes → apply structural changes
(detach, spawn, respawn) → race progress → emit ordered events → publish snapshot when a buffer is free. Persistently unplayable lag
enters `performance-stall` at the last completed tick; never enlarge `dt`, skip ticks, delete debris or refuse joins.

Determinism (plan §7.2): seeded RNG streams, stable iteration order, no wall clock in the sim, Rapier `enhanced-determinism`. Same-build
same-target runs produce identical full-state hashes. Native vs WASM physics identity is a **measured** claim checked where the fixtures live
(S01 runner, S02 worker, S03 feel bank): target identical full-state hashes; if they differ, record where they diverge and compare feel
scenarios by envelopes and discrete events (detach, lap, finish) instead, and say so in the receipt. Canonical **map bytes** must match
native vs WASM exactly, always.

Rapier footguns to re-verify on Rust 0.36 (plan §6.1, Spike C used the JS API): `update_vehicle` doesn't wake a sleeping chassis;
brake is an impulse per tick, engine force is a force; external forces fight the wheel-slip model. Engineering rule (AGENTS.md): use
Rapier's vehicle controller as documented for the pinned version; never multiply/divide by large factors "to make it work"; sustained
forces integrate with `dt` once; impulses apply once. Document findings in code and `docs/learnings/sim.md`.

- Rapier world from `jj.map.v1`: heightfield, barriers, dressing colliders from the **kit registry's collider proxies** (§8.1, `assets/kit/`).
- Raycast vehicle from a vehicle profile: a **provisional profile with Spike J's Cruze dimensions** until P1-V02's sidecar exists (P1-S03
  switches to the sidecar).
- Seeded RNG streams; full-state hash; **applied-tick input journal** (the one sim funnel: phones, pads, keys, autopilot, test bots and
  replays all enter as applied-tick inputs; nothing changes sim state except journaled setup commands).

title: P1-S02 · Sim worker (WASM) and lifecycle
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S02** (cites §4.4, §7.1, §7.3a); master cut V2-06, V2-119 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D1` · **Track:** `sim` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S01, P1-N06, P1-N07a. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Run `jj-session` + `jj-input` + `jj-sim` as WASM in a host Web Worker that owns the 120 Hz clock, decodes controller bytes itself, publishes
pooled snapshots and ordered events, and pauses/resumes correctly when the host tab hides. Rendering rate never changes the simulation.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-wasm-host/`, `web/host/src/worker/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Rendering (R01/R02), host pads/keys sampling (C05), test messages (F05b), map preparation flow wiring (G01, M08a).

## Contract and design decisions
Time and ticks (plan §7.1): 120 Hz fixed step, `dt = 1/120` (R61). The worker owns the accumulator and steps whole ticks; rendering
interpolates between the last two snapshots. **Tick order:** apply commands and inputs due at this tick → set vehicle controls and surface
friction → `update_vehicle` against current query data → `step` → read contact data and build damage episodes → apply structural changes
(detach, spawn, respawn) → race progress → emit ordered events → publish snapshot when a buffer is free. Persistently unplayable lag
enters `performance-stall` at the last completed tick; never enlarge `dt`, skip ticks, delete debris or refuse joins.

Worker ABI (plan §4.4; see P1-N01 for the full table): main → sim `Init`, `NetBytes`, `LocalSource`, `Ui`, `Lifecycle`, `MapReady`,
`ReturnBuffer`; sim → main `Snapshot` (transferable), `Events` (ordered), `Journal`, `Outbound`.
- Controller bytes are decoded by `jj-protocol` and interpreted by `jj-input` **inside the worker**, the same path as `LocalSource`.
- Worker-owned 120 Hz scheduler; **pooled transferable snapshots** (bulk binary, no per-entity calls); if no pooled buffer is free the worker
  skips that publish and never blocks physics or drops events.
- **Pause reasons** compose: `manual`, `host-hidden`, `renderer-unavailable`, `performance-stall`, `fault`. Hidden time is never replayed;
  resume goes through a short visible countdown with input re-armed at neutral. Controller loss never pauses (R45).
- Interpolation pairs come from the same round/life (never interpolate across a respawn).
- A worker panic / unrecoverable WASM error = the `fault` pause reason (the host shows "Something broke" with Save bug clip / New room; R84).
Determinism (plan §7.2): seeded RNG streams, stable iteration order, no wall clock in the sim, Rapier `enhanced-determinism`. Same-build
same-target runs produce identical full-state hashes. Native vs WASM physics identity is a **measured** claim checked where the fixtures live
(S01 runner, S02 worker, S03 feel bank): target identical full-state hashes; if they differ, record where they diverge and compare feel
scenarios by envelopes and discrete events (detach, lap, finish) instead, and say so in the receipt. Canonical **map bytes** must match
native vs WASM exactly, always.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: S01 core, N06 input, N07a seats.
- Provides: the worker to F05b, R01 (replaces the synthetic snapshot source), C05, G00→G04, S03 (WASM parity through `jj-wasm-host` in Node).

## Required tests
Browser tests (Playwright):
- rendering at 30/60/144 Hz gives the same tick hash for the same inputs (hash table);
- §7.3a `source-parity`: the same tick inputs from controller bytes vs `LocalSource` give the same result;
- hiding the tab pauses with no catch-up; resume shows a countdown with neutral re-arm;
- starving snapshot buffers never blocks physics.

In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Test output; hash table. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-S02/`.

title: P1-S03 · Vehicle feel bank
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S03** (cites §7.3, §7.3a, §13b.1, §14); master cut V2-40, V2-41a (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D1` · **Track:** `sim` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S01, P1-S02, P1-V02, P1-F05a. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
A drivable, fun-first Cruz Missile: the §7.3 behaviours as scenario-bank cases with outcome signatures, the S03-owned affordance rows, the
authority metric and `jj sim --sweep` for tuning, built from the baked V02 sidecar. This is the baseline the owner drives first in G04's free
drive; the skill-payoff duels are P1-S09 so free drive doesn't wait for the hardest tuning.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/src/vehicle/`, `scenarios/feel/`, `scenarios/affordances/` (S03 rows), `assets/profiles/cruz-missile.json`, `jj sim --sweep`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Duels (S09), damage rows (S04*), recovery rows (S05), utility rows (S08), production sidecar re-run (V03 re-runs this bank).

## Contract and design decisions
Vehicle feel (plan §7.3; targets are TUNE, judged at G-FEEL):
| Affordance | DEFAULT starting behaviour | Scenario |
|---|---|---|
| Suspension | Soft springs, strong damping, visible roll/squat/dive, single-settle landings | `idle-settle`, `jump-land` |
| Steer/throttle/brake/reverse | DRIVE X steers; up throttles; down brakes, reversing near rest | `progressive-brake`, `slalom` |
| Handbrake drift | ACTION left: rear friction slip × 0.35, 0.4 s smooth recovery; drifting charges boost | `drift-entry-exit` |
| Boost | ACTION right: meter 0–1, drains 0.35/s, recharges 0.12/s, +60 % engine force | `boost-hold` |
| Wheelie ("lift and launch", R64) | DRIVE pulled past full brake (y < −0.85) preloads; release = leaving the preload zone and passing y > −0.3 within 250 ms; lift scales with preload time (max at 0.4 s); held past 1.2 s cancels; needs ≥ 3 wheels grounded. Payoff (DEFAULT, TUNE): well-timed release (preload 0.35–1.2 s) adds +15 % drive force for 0.8 s and lifts the front enough to hop kerb-height obstacles and small debris; an early release only lifts a little; a late one does nothing; steering reduced while the front is up | `wheelie-ok`, `wheelie-fail`, `brake-no-wheelie` |
| Air control | Mild pitch/roll torque from DRIVE while airborne | `air-level` |
| Surfaces | Per surface ID friction multipliers: tarmac 1.0, packed dirt 0.8, gravel 0.7, rock 0.9 | `surface-deltas` |

Affordance bank (plan §7.3a): each row is a scenario-bank case in `scenarios/affordances/` with an outcome signature, run from several
starting states and compared with mash, hold and no-input baselines. Numbers are TUNE envelopes set at the first accepted playtest.
Each row also gets the §13b.1 four-step check when its tuning changes: (1) replay to show determinism; (2) change one input timing or
parameter to show agency and a causal difference; (3) debug-only ablations and solver stress (more substeps/iterations, high speed) to reject
numerical accidents; (4) the owner playtests. Mash and no-input baselines must differ from deliberate driving.

S03-owned affordance rows:
| The player can… | Scenario |
|---|---|
| Go forward and backward from rest, on every surface, without an accidental wheelie or stunt | `fwd-back-rest` |
| Stop: progressive braking reaches a stop within an envelope from 10/20/30 m/s | `brake-stop` |
| Turn around inside the road width (three-point turn) | `turn-around` |
| Reverse out of a nose-in wall or barrier contact within 2 s | `unstick-wall` |
| Steer with authority at 5/15/30 m/s and counter-steer out of a slide | `authority`, `slalom` |
| Enter and leave a drift on purpose, and gain boost from it | `drift-entry-exit` |
| Go meaningfully faster with boost than without, and boost-forever isn't the best line | `boost-line` |
| Wheelie only from the pull-release gesture, never from braking | `wheelie-ok`, `brake-no-wheelie` |
| Level the car in the air and land a jump on its wheels | `air-level`, `jump-land` (M03d shares) |
| Get back onto the route from the verge or a ditch | `rejoin-route` |

**Authority metric** (re-expressed from 0.1 `static/js/systems/steeringAuthority.js`, `tests/unit/steering-authority.test.js`): heading change
from full steer in 0.5 s at 5/15/30 m/s. `jj sim --sweep PARAM=A..B` over profile parameters → CSV (S03 adds the flag to F05a's `jj sim`).
Every scenario carries an outcome signature; each tuning change follows the §13b.1 four-step check. Owner feel verdicts from G04 (round
records) are inputs, never gates.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: S01, S02 (WASM build through `jj-wasm-host` in Node), V02 sidecar, F05a surface.
- Provides: the tuned profile + feel bank to G04 (free drive), S04a (damage needs a drivable car), S05, S08, S09, V03, Q02 (accepted baseline).

## Reuses / gap
Reuses S01's runner/scenario format and F05a's surface; 0.1's authority metric idea. Gap: no tuned, measured vehicle feel.

## Required tests
- Scenario bank `crates/jj-sim/tests/feel.rs` + `scenarios/feel/*.json` for every §7.3 scenario, native and through the WASM build in Node.
- Affordance rows above from several starting states vs mash/hold/no-input baselines.
- One `jj sim --sweep` CSV committed as evidence.
