title: P1-S04 · Damage: loose, detach, debris, wreck (epic)
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S04** (cites §6.3, §7.3a, §13b.1); master cut V2-60/62/63 slice, R86 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D3` · **Track:** `sim` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S03, P1-V03. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Epic for R86 damage in Playtest 1: parts go intact → loose → detached, debris persists dynamically for the round, wrecks respawn in ~2 s.
Split along master §18.4's order: episode attribution → part damage (S04a) → safe hinge/detach/mass update (S04b) → wrecks and
persistent-body qualification (S04c). Consumers (G05, Q01) depend on this epic, i.e. on all three children.

## Scope (owned paths)
Children own `crates/jj-sim/src/damage/` and `scenarios/damage/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Rendering of loose/detached parts (R02 supports it from synthetic snapshots; V03 provides dark bays and hinge data).

## Contract and design decisions
Damage model (plan §6.3, R86): each part goes **intact → loose → detached**. No dents.
- **Health** (DEFAULT/TUNE): `front` 100, `back` 100, each door 60, each wheel 80.
- **Damage episodes:** every part is its own collider on the chassis body, so a contact's collider handle names the part. Per (car, part,
  other body), aggregate normal impulses over a **50 ms** game-time window; count only contacts with closing speed **≥ 4 m/s** (TUNE),
  excluding resting and suspension support. Damage = `k_part × Σ impulse`. Calibrate `k` with scenarios, not formulas:
  | Scenario | Expected |
  |---|---|
  | `bump-4`: 4 m/s nudge into another car | no damage |
  | `rest-60`: parked against a wall for 60 s | no damage |
  | `side-swipe-8`: 8 m/s door-to-door | that door goes loose, nothing detaches |
  | `wall-head-on-15`: 15 m/s into a wall | `front` detaches |
  | `t-bone-12`: 12 m/s into a door | that door detaches |
  | `wheel-kerb-12`: 12 m/s wheel strike on a barrier end | that wheel goes loose |
- **Wheel colliders:** small cylinders/balls at each hub, in a collision group that **excludes terrain and road**, so wheel strikes from
  cars/debris/barriers register without fighting the raycast suspension.
- **Loose** (health ≤ 50 %): the part stays attached and its collider stays at the attached pose. `jj-sim` integrates a damped 1-DOF spring
  about the part's hinge axis, driven by chassis acceleration (deterministic, in snapshots, replayable). Limits: doors 0–70° about the front
  edge; bumpers hang 0–25° about their top edge; wheels wobble ±6° camber. A loose wheel loses 15 % friction slip (TUNE). Visual springs, not
  joints (joints risk injecting energy, Spike I).
- **Detached** (health 0): at the end of the tick remove the part's collider from the chassis, create a dynamic body with the part's proxy
  and mass at its current world pose, set velocity to the chassis velocity at that point (`v + ω × r`) plus a small outward kick, recompute
  chassis mass properties. A detached wheel disables that wheel in the vehicle controller (zero suspension force, friction and engine
  force; verify the Rapier 0.36 API) so that corner drops onto its collider.
- **Debris persists** for the round as dynamic bodies that may sleep and wake (R58, R66): no TTL, cap, static conversion or merging.
- **Wreck:** ≥ 2 wheels detached, or stuck/flipped past the recovery timeout, or out of bounds. Remaining parts pop off as debris and the
  **husk stays as a dynamic body** (DEFAULT, Q-A2). After ~2 s (R20) the player respawns at their own legal recovery anchor in a fresh
  intact car with the same identity and progress.
- **Rendering:** loose = the part's instance with the hinge rotation applied; detached = the same part-type instance with a physics-driven
  matrix; a missing part shows the core's dark bay; detached parts keep the owner's paint colour.

## Interfaces
- Children inherit this epic's external deps (S03, V03). Provides damage state in snapshots/events to R02, R09, G05, A03.

## Required tests
See children. The epic closes when S04a, S04b and S04c close (the verifier closes epics via `br epic close-eligible`).

P1-S04a, P1-S04b and P1-S04c are closed; together they deliver the §6.3 model with its calibration scenarios, energy checks and the `control-after-hit`, `loose-wheel-drive`, `two-wheels-off` and `debris-pile-exit` affordance rows.

title: P1-S04b · Loose springs, detach and persistent debris
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S04b** (cites §6.3, §13b.1); master cut V2-62 slice (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D3` · **Track:** `sim` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S04a. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Make damage visible and physical: loose parts swing on deterministic springs, detached parts become dynamic debris with inherited velocity,
mass updates are exact, and nothing ever deletes, merges, freezes or budgets debris. Energy accounting proves the springs and kicks don't
inject energy.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/src/damage/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Wrecks/husks/respawn (S04c). Rendering (R02/V03).

## Contract and design decisions
- Hinge springs: damped 1-DOF about each part's hinge axis, driven by chassis acceleration; deterministic; published in snapshots; limits
  doors 0–70° about the front edge, bumpers 0–25° about their top edge, wheels ±6° camber; a loose wheel loses 15 % friction slip (TUNE).
- Detach at the end of the tick with `v + ω × r` + a small outward kick; chassis mass recompute; detached-wheel disable in the vehicle
  controller (verify the Rapier 0.36 API; S01's fixture pins how).
- Debris persists for the round as dynamic bodies that may sleep and wake: **no static conversion, deletion, merging or count budget
  anywhere** (R58, R66).
- **Energy accounting** (§13b.1): `Δ(kinetic + potential) − authorised work` stays under a solver-calibrated tolerance; a positive residual
  is a bug candidate.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: S04a part states. Provides: detach events + debris bodies to S04c, S09 (detached door for the hop duel), R02/R09/G05.

## Reuses / gap
Reuses Spike C (detach → dynamic debris in Rapier works: velocity + angular transfer, mass removed, sleeps, wakes on contact) and Spike I (springs not joints). Gap: none of it exists in Rust.

## Required tests
- Scenario bank: detached parts inherit velocity, stay dynamic, sleep and wake on contact at round end; mass totals before/after.
- A grep + test proving no static conversion, deletion, merging or count budget.
- Energy accounting for loose springs, detach kicks and a 20-part debris pile, including a solver-stress rerun with doubled substeps.
- §7.3a `loose-wheel-drive`.

title: P1-S05 · Race rules and recovery
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S05** (cites §7.4, §7.5, §14); master cut V2-73a, V2-102 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D1` · **Track:** `sim` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S01, P1-M01, P1-F05a. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Legal progress, recovery and race completion in the sim: gates in order, anchors, flip assist, Recover, out-of-bounds, laps, the finish
window, the absolute deadline and finished-car ghosting. "Out of bounds always recovers" is a 0.1 lesson kept.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/src/race/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Placement and drop-in (S06), autopilot (S07), results/points (N07c), wreck mechanics (S04c).

## Contract and design decisions
Recovery and race rules (plan §7.4–§7.5):
- **Flip assist** (load-bearing, Spike C: a rounded cabin doesn't self-right at these proportions): when up·Y < 0.2 and speed < 2 m/s for
  1 s, apply a visible self-right torque; if still inverted 3 s after the assist starts (4 s after coming to rest inverted), the car is wrecked.
- **Recover** button: available when speed < 3 m/s for 1 s or inverted; 2 s penalty; respawn at the own anchor.
- **Out of bounds:** below the kill height or outside map bounds → wreck → respawn.
- **Route** = the map's centerline with checkpoint gates (~every 40 m). Legal progress needs gates in order; the **recovery anchor** is the last
  gate passed, offset onto the centerline at a clear pose. Never use raw nearest-spline projection at crossings/shortcuts.
- **Race end:** 3 laps DEFAULT; a 30 s window after the first finisher; absolute deadline `max(180 s, 2 × laps × refLap)` from countdown
  completion; finished cars stop colliding with racers (and debris) and coast on autopilot (keep terrain collision and their tile);
  unfinished cars rank by legal progress (master §10.12).

Re-express from 0.1 (§14): `tests/e2e/oob-recovery.spec.ts` (out-of-bounds always recovers) as a Rust scenario.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: S01, M01 (route, gates, bounds), F05a. Provides: progress/anchors to S06, S07, N07c, R07 (HUD lap/position), G01 (JN2).

## Required tests
Scenario bank `crates/jj-sim/tests/race.rs`: OOB always recovers; a flip from 12 inverted poses rights itself or is wrecked within 4 s of
coming to rest; a shortcut across the infield doesn't count progress; the first finisher starts the window; an all-stuck race ends at the
deadline; §7.3a `flip-recover`, `oob-recover`.

description:

## Purpose and observable outcome
One placement service for start grids, respawns and drop-in that works for any N with no cap, queue or refusal: the old 0.1 silent spawn cap
must never return. Late joiners land ~3 s behind the last racer with that car's lap/gate state.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/src/placement/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Wreck triggers (S04c), the browser-side drop-in journey (G02).

## Contract and design decisions
Placement service (plan §7.5; one service for start grid, respawn and drop-in): commit placements at tick boundaries against current cars and
debris; **1.5 s spawn protection** disables car/debris contacts (terrain and barriers stay solid) and only ends in a non-overlapping pose.
**Start grid for any N without a cap or queue:** rows fill the map's declared start corridor back along the route; once the corridor is full,
further cars are placed in it anyway under spawn protection (ghosted against cars and debris) and turn solid only when clear. Nobody waits,
is refused or is dropped. **Drop-in (R63):** a new seat spawns ~3 s of route behind the last still-racing car, with that car's lap/gate state,
marked as a late joiner (master §10.9: use a short history of the last racer's validated progress; before enough history exists, place after
the actual last entrant near the start; a stationary last racer still gets a positive gap). Reconnect and wreck use the seat's own anchor.
If the ordinary pose search fails the entrant still gets an immediately controllable protected car (master §6.5).

Re-express from 0.1 (§14): `static/js/resources/SpawnAllocator.js`, `SpawnGenerator.js`, `tests/unit/spawn-allocator.test.js`,
`spawn-generation.test.js`, `spawn-cap-regression.test.js`: spawn poses for any N without overlap; the old silent spawn cap must never return.

title: P1-S09 · Skill-payoff duels
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S09** (cites §7.3b, §13b.1); master cut V2-40/V2-41a part, owner 2026-10-02 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D3` · **Track:** `sim` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S03, P1-S04b. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Prove that doing techniques **well pays off, badly costs, and none dominates** (owner: "the drifting player around a corner beats the
normal player"; "the forward/back wheelie beats players when executed perfectly vs not"). Mash never wins.

## Scope (owned paths)
`scenarios/duels/`, `crates/jj-sim/src/vehicle/` (tuning only), `assets/profiles/cruz-missile.json`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The drivable baseline (S03); the cone-defence duel (S08). L-plates reuse these duels later (Full, R64).

## Contract and design decisions
Each duel runs identical cars on the same greybox segment from the same state with scripted inputs: a **plain** line, a **well-executed**
technique (timing found by `jj sim --sweep`, then frozen in the fixture) and a **botched** one (too early, too late or held too long). The
assertion is an ordering on time to a gate after the segment, with TUNE margins.
| Duel | Expect |
|---|---|
| `drift-corner-duel` (hairpin at 18 m/s entry) | well-timed drift + its banked boost beats brake-and-steer; a mistimed drift loses or spins |
| `drift-boost-chain` (S-bend then straight) | drifting both bends and spending the boost on the straight beats a grip driver over the sector |
| `drift-straight-penalty` | drifting down a straight is slower than driving it straight |
| `wheelie-launch-duel` (from 0 and from 8 m/s) | a well-timed pull-release launch beats plain full throttle to a gate 40 m on; early release no better than plain; late/held worse |
| `wheelie-hop-duel` (a kerb or a detached door across the line) | the hop clears it and keeps speed; plain driving hits it and loses speed |
| `boost-placement-duel` | the same boost spent on the straight beats it spent into a corner |
| `air-control-duel` (greybox jump) | levelling lands on its wheels and keeps speed; no input lands nose-first and loses more; over-correcting is worst |
| `mash-duel` | in each duel above, a mash script never beats the well-executed line |
Every tuning change follows the §13b.1 four-step check and must keep every S03 and S04 affordance row passing. The owner's G04 feel notes
(round records) are inputs; margins are decided by the owner's feel verdict at playtests.

## Interfaces

title: P1-S10 · Derby rules and damage-point scoring
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S10** (cites master §10.9, §10.12; R56; owner 2026-10-03); master cut V2-105 + V2-126 derby slice (owner 2026-10-03) (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D6` · **Track:** `sim` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S04, P1-S06, P1-N07c, P1-M10. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
The derby game rules in the sim and session: a 3-minute round won on damage dealt to opponents, with honest attribution so self-wrecks, spawn
protection and the environment never score, fast respawn, and late joiners welcome.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/src/derby/` (attribution, round clock), `crates/jj-session/src/results/` (derby classification), `scenarios/derby/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The arena (P1-M10); the Overview camera (P1-R11); round-loop wiring and the lobby mode choice (P1-G06); last-man-standing (P1-S11).

## Contract and design decisions
Owner direction 2026-10-03: the first derby is **passive containment** (the bowl's walls and lip keep cars in; **no shrinking
wall** or other arena-closing mechanism) and is **won on damage dealt** (R56: a 3-minute round ranked by raw damage points; late joiners are
allowed and simply have less time). A **last-man-standing** mode comes later (P1-S11, deferred) with a host switch for drop-in while playing.

Derby raw points (master §10.12): each accepted HP of opponent damage gives 1 point, a detach gives +5 and a wreck +20, once per
part/life event. Self, friendly-fire, spawn-protected and environmental damage give zero. Integer damage units of 0.001 HP and score units of
1/2000 point: normal damage earns twice its damage units; bonuses are exact integers. Autopilot halves the credited event once, so a 10 HP +
detach + wreck episode gives 35 human points or 17.5 autopilot points. The sim records control mode at the causal action, not at display time.
Secondary debris attribution expires 3 s game time after the last qualifying instigator impulse; after that it's environmental. Equal raw scores
share rank; championship conversion uses the same table as Race (`[25,18,15,12,10,8,6,4,2,1]`, then 1 for every later rank) with no finish bonus.
Combo callouts are presentation only (no multiplier).

- Round: 3 minutes on game time (paused with game time), ranked by raw points; equal raw scores share rank.
- Respawn after a wreck in ~2 s at a safe edge pose through the placement service (arena policy), with spawn protection (no damage dealt or
  taken while protected).
- Late joiners (R56): allowed at any time, spawn at a safe edge pose, score from when they arrive; no normalisation.
- Damage itself comes from the S04 model (intact → loose → detached, husks stay, debris stays dynamic); S10 only attributes and scores it.

## Interfaces
- Consumes: S04 damage episodes, S06 placement, N07c results. Provides: derby facts (points, events) in snapshots/events to R11's HUD bands, G06, A03 cues.

## Reuses / gap
Reuses S04's contact episodes (adds the instigator to each) and N07c's classification. Gap: no attribution or derby scoring.

## Required tests
- Fixture: the master example: a 10 HP + detach + wreck episode scores 35 human points and 17.5 autopilot points.
- Fixtures: self-damage, spawn-protected and environmental damage score zero; debris attribution expires after 3 s; equal raw scores share rank.
- A late joiner's ranking uses raw points; the 3-minute clock pauses with game time.

In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

title: P1-S11 · Last-man-standing derby mode with a drop-in switch (later)
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S11** (cites owner 2026-10-03; master §10.9, §10.12); master cut new (owner 2026-10-03) (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).

**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-G06. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Status notes
**Deferred by the owner (2026-10-03): "a mode for later".** Created deferred so it's tracked; `br undefer` it when the owner wants it.

## Purpose and observable outcome
A second derby mode: wrecked cars are out (no respawn) and the last car running wins, with a host switch for whether new players may drop in
while a round is running.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/src/derby/` (elimination), `crates/jj-session/src/director/` (mode rule, drop-in switch), `web/host/src/round/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The damage-points derby (S10/G06).

## Contract and design decisions
- **Last man standing:** a wreck eliminates that car for the round (its husk and debris stay, R58); the round ends when one car is left running,
  or at the deadline (rank by survival order, then raw damage points). Eliminated players stay in the room and watch (and drive in the warm-up if
  the owner wants that).
- **"Drop in while playing" switch** (host setting, next-round effect): **on** → a new player enters the running round at a safe edge pose like
  any derby late joiner; **off** → a new player joins the room at once, gets their seat, number and colour, and enters at the next round. "Off" is
  a mode rule, never a cap: nobody is refused, queued for capacity or limited in number (R36, R66).
- Scoring and results reuse S10's attribution.

## Required tests
- Fixtures: elimination on wreck; the round ends with one car left; survival-order ranking with raw-point tie-break.
- Journey: drop-in on vs off (a joiner enters the running round vs at the next round, seated immediately either way).

title: P1-S12 · Filler bots for small groups
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-S12** (cites master §10.12 (Teams and fillers); R45); master cut V2-42 + V2-75 fillers slice (owner 2026-10-03) (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `D8` · **Track:** `sim` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S07, P1-S10, P1-G06, P1-W01. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
So two or three people still get a lively race or derby: the host can fill the field with visibly marked bots that drive, ram and use items.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/src/bots/`, `crates/jj-session/src/director/` (filler target), `web/host/src/ui/` (setting + bot badge).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Dropout autopilot (S07), which stays weak and only drives for absent players.

## Contract and design decisions
- Host setting **"Fill to N with bots"** (next-round effect, default off): `max(0, N − humans)` bot entrants at preparation. It's a filler
  target, never an admission limit: human joins never wait for bots, and excess bots leave at the next round boundary, never by deleting a
  racing car or its debris (master §10.12).
- Bots are visibly marked, have no ballot or Ready, never count towards the start condition, and appear in round results with separate bot
  standings (human event points are computed among humans).
- Driving: race bots follow the route with a skill setting (low/medium); derby bots seek and ram nearby cars and back off when stuck; bots use
  held items with simple rules (boomerang at a car in front or behind, sanga when about to be rammed). Same physics and inputs as humans.

## Required tests
- Scenarios: a 1-human + 5-bot race finishes with bots spread across the field; a derby with bots scores; a human joining mid-round never waits; bots leave at the next boundary when humans fill the field.

title: P1-U01 · Design guide and tokens
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-U01** (cites §3a, §13b.4; experience direction §2–§3); master cut new (owner 2026-10-02); master §12.1, §12.6 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `POC` · **Track:** `design` · **Machine:** `on:any` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** none; can start immediately.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Settle the visual language every UI task builds from, before any UI code exists (G-DESIGN, owner ruling 2026-10-02). The
output is a design guide plus **tokens as data** (`tokens.json` + schema), brand files, a component sheet, identity-under-stress
checks, a copy voice and at least three H4-style frames. C01 and D05 start from the *draft* tokens immediately; every other UI
task (C02–C04, C06, C07, R04, R06–R10) waits for the owner's verdict at P1-U04 and then builds against the accepted copy in
`art/ui/accepted/<date>/`. Observable outcome: an agent can render any UI element from `tokens.json` alone, and every listed
check passes as a scripted run.

## Scope (owned paths)
`art/ui/GUIDE.md`, `art/ui/tokens.json` (+ its JSON schema), `art/ui/fonts/`, `art/ui/frames/` (style frames and their prompts), `art/style/MASTER_PROMPTS.md` (UI block and the supersession note).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
TV mocks (P1-U02), phone mocks (P1-U03), the in-world look and motion reel (P1-U05), the gallery and verdict (P1-U04). Turning tokens into CSS variables and shared components is P1-C01. No game code.

## Contract and design decisions
Style references (owner, 2026-10-02): **most authoritative** is the H4 round-highlights image
`docs/plans/ux-study-2026-09-29/images/H4-host-round-results-v2.png` (ink-and-cream comic panels, bold condensed headings,
yellow and cobalt accents, a painted outback world behind the chrome). The ute with the bullbar (H1, M1) shows where the
roster goes; a ute in a style frame isn't a defect. Brand badges that image generation adds (M1's grille) are placeholders
and never ship (`art/style/MASTER_PROMPTS.md` guards). **Superseded:** the drivers'-heads-out cartoony look
(`art/style/refs/ui_lobby.png`). In-game tiles in the mocks show the real Cruz Missile (Spike J,
`spikes/art-pipeline/J-cruze-lowpoly/`) because that's what Playtest 1 renders.

**Tokens as data** (`art/ui/tokens.json`, validated by a JSON schema committed beside it):
- palette with hex values and **named contrast pairs** (text/background) that the check script reads;
- an **identity palette** giving every seat a distinct colour + number for any N: numbers carry identity past the palette;
  colours are reused with distinct numbers as N grows (no cap, R66). Patterns are Full (plan §2.3), so colour + number must hold;
- two **self-hosted OFL fonts** (a condensed display face and a body face) with licence files and subsets; stable/tabular digits
  for scores, positions and countdowns (experience direction §2); no remote font service (R70);
- a **type scale per viewing profile** (TV at 3 m, desk, handheld), spacing scale, a **minimum touch target**, a **TV-safe margin**;
- ink-outline weight and the **panel wobble** spec (master §12.1: a few px at TV scale, consistent per element, never animated,
  text and hit boxes stay straight);
- icons; **motion durations** and their reduced-motion variants (U05 builds the reel from these).

**Guide** (`GUIDE.md`): the identity kit (number badge, colour, name, tile badge, Identify pulse; master §5.1–§5.2) and how the
UI chrome frames the 3D world (the in-world look itself is U05). It names a reference image for each element.

**Brand:** one wordmark (SVG), an app icon and favicon, and the **QR rule**: a plain high-contrast code with its full quiet zone
and nothing in the middle (H2's kangaroo hurts scanning), with the room code beside it in the display face.

**Components:** a sheet of every component in every state: primary, secondary and destructive buttons, panels, badges, toasts,
confirmations, progress/loading, error, disabled, and **focus for keyboard and gamepad** (experience direction §3: focus styles,
screen-reader labels and keyboard/gamepad selection are real states, not polish).

**Identity under stress:** the identity palette checked under colour-vision-deficiency simulation (protanopia, deuteranopia,
tritanopia), with numbers carrying identity wherever colours collide; 3-digit numbers; 32-grapheme names (master §10.6 limit);
non-Latin names (font coverage and a named fallback).

**Copy voice:** a short UI copy guide and glossary: one word each for room, game, seat and car; Australian spelling; button verbs;
tone consistent with P1-A00's announcer copy (`docs/copy/australianisms.md` once it exists).

**Controller in a dim room:** base colour and brightness chosen for a dark living room (DEFAULT: ink/navy base, cream panels,
the player's colour; §3a).

**Style frames:** at least three in the H4 style (the TV in-race grid with HUD, the lobby at 32, the phone controller), made
through the art pipeline (MASTER_PROMPTS + the UI block, via `codex exec`; omit `--model`), prompts committed, generated vehicles
and badges marked as placeholders. Mark `art/style/refs/ui_lobby.png` superseded in MASTER_PROMPTS.

§3a starting proposals (DEFAULT; the POC designs and shows each as ONE worked proposal with a one-line why; owner
2026-10-03: "don't give me choices on things that are obvious"; alternatives stay in evidence folders, not the gallery):
- Lobby: the warm-up drive behind the QR and player strip (plan §9).
- Grids with a gap: balanced rows first; the last row is centred and its tiles grow wider within the aspect band, so gameplay
  area comes first (master §6.2); any cell still left over shows the join QR and live standings, never black.
- Cameras: third person by default, first person per seat from the controller (master §6.3); mocks show a mixed grid.
- In-world look: master §12.1's comic treatment (faceted cars, 2–3 tone toon ramp, ink outlines, halftone in shadows); if its
  cost at 24 tiles is too high, present the cheapest version that keeps the look (e.g. outlines on cars and debris only) and say why.
- Controller in a dark room: ink/navy base with cream panels and the player's colour; the TV keeps H4's cream panels.
- Lobby at 32 and beyond: compact roster cards (number badge, colour, name, Ready) that reflow into more columns down to the
  guide's legible minimum, then compact to number + name chips. Never a "max players".

## Interfaces
- Provides: `art/ui/tokens.json` (draft) → P1-C01 (CSS variables + `web/shared/ui/`), P1-D05 (index styling), P1-U02/U03/U05
  (mocks built from tokens); later the accepted copy in `art/ui/accepted/<date>/` (P1-U04) for every UI task.
- Provides: the guide's minimum cap height / touch target / TV-safe margin, which U02/U03/R07/C02 measure against.

## Required tests
- A scripted token check (any small script under `art/ui/`, run in the wave): schema validation of `tokens.json`; WCAG AA
  contrast for every named text/background pair at its intended size; it exits non-zero naming the failing pair.
- A CVD simulation sheet generated from the identity palette (protanopia/deuteranopia/tritanopia) showing every pair of
  adjacent seats told apart by colour or number.
- A font render check of the stress names (3-digit numbers, 32 graphemes, non-Latin) with the bundled fonts or the named fallback.
- Fresh-eyes review note (§13b.4) by a reviewer that isn't the implementer: images opened at gameplay size, H4 as the named
  reference, elements present/absent, first-look reading, defects.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
Guide + tokens + component sheet + CVD sheet + frames + check output + review note. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-U01/`.

## How this bead closes
- `ev:ci`: green Gitea CI on a commit containing this bead, cited as `receipt:<run url>` with a `batch_verify` gate pass (before CI exists, a committed local receipt; while CI is down, the verifier's `batch-verify.sh` receipt).

## Working rules

- [x] [ev:ci] The identity palette's CVD simulation sheet (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia) shows every pair of adjacent seats told apart by colour or number.
- [x] [ev:ci] The two display/body fonts are local OFL files with licences and subsets, and they (or the named fallback) render the stress names: 3-digit numbers, 32-grapheme names, non-Latin names.

title: P1-U02 · TV mocks: grid, HUD, lobby and results
description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-U02** (cites §3a items 2–7, 12, 14; §9; §10); master cut new (owner 2026-10-02); master §6.2, §6.3, §6.4, §10.6, §10.8 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).
**Drop:** `POC` · **Track:** `design` · **Machine:** `on:mac` · **Evidence kinds:** `ev:ci`, `ev:hardware`
**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-U01. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
Show the owner, on the TCL from the couch, exactly how the TV will look before R04/R06/R07/R08/R09 build it: the grid as players
join and leave (1 → 32 → 1), grids with a gap, the per-tile HUD over **live moving tiles**, mixed FP/TP tiles, the lobby at
2/8/16/32, Minimum results, the host's own controls, caption placement, the over-3D overlays and (as a design reference only)
the derby Overview. The HUD is built the way the game will build it, so its frame cost is measured, not guessed. The accepted
mocks become the named references R-tasks are judged against.

## Scope (owned paths)
`art/ui/poc/tv/` (static HTML/CSS/JS built from `tokens.json`; three.js for the live tiles, bundled locally, no CDN).

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Phone mocks (U03); the in-world look and motion reel (U05; U05 renders on top of these mocks); the gallery/publication (U04). Building the derby Overview is Full (V2-22) and its scenarios (`derby-overview-8/24`) stay there.

## Contract and design decisions
Static HTML/CSS/JS layout mocks built from `tokens.json` at **1920×1080 and 3840×2160**, plus **21:9** and a **portrait phone host**
for the grid. They show §3a items 2–7, 12 and 14:
- a **grid player** that adds and removes players 1 → 32 → 1 with the animated reflow (seat order kept; only joins and leaves
  reflow, master §6.2), with the layout rule written next to it as **pseudocode** (it becomes P1-R04's contract once accepted).
  Master §6.2 rule to start from: choose rows × cols with rows·cols ≥ N minimising unused area, tile aspect in a playable band
  (~1.2–2.0 third person; FP a little narrower), any display aspect (portrait stacks vertically, ultrawide adds columns), spare
  cells show a filler (QR "join now", standings), never black; resizing animated (~300 ms ease) when N changes; for N = 2
  evaluate horizontal and vertical splits; playable area and own-car readability outrank filler panels;
- the **gap cases** N = 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 13 handled the §3a way (balanced rows; last row centred with wider tiles; leftovers show
  QR + standings);
- the **per-tile HUD**: number badge, name, position, lap, boost meter, wreck/respawn countdown, autopilot and reconnecting
  badges, Identify pulse and outline, the countdown overlay; at the smallest tile (32 tiles at 1080p) and the largest;
- **first- and third-person tiles mixed** in one grid (FP shows a bonnet edge, master §6.3);
- the **lobby** with the warm-up behind it at 2, 8, 16 and 32 players plus the rule for larger N (never a "max players");
- **Minimum results/intermission** at 8 and 32 players: race rematch, reel area, timer, QR, Hide replay / Start next round now /
  Return to lobby (H4's layout without Full's voting);
- the **host's own controls**: Start now, End and Disband with confirmation, pause, the pad/keyboard input drawer, the diagnostics
  overlay, and how they stay out of the way during a race;
- where the announcer's **captions** sit (A03) without covering anyone's HUD;
- the **overlays drawn over the 3D view**: nameplates over other cars, the Identify outline, the off-screen arrow to your own car;
- the **derby Overview** (master §6.4) as a forward design reference: a live greybox bowl with 8, 16 and 32 cars framed by the
  cars' bounding box at a fixed pitch (≈55–65°), never rotating; identity rings and nameplates scaled by camera distance; the HUD
  in thin edge bands (3-minute timer and damage-points standings); the host's Grid ↔ Overview switch. Design only.

**Tiles are live, never stills:** Spike J's Cruz Missile (`spikes/art-pipeline/J-cruze-lowpoly/`) driving scripted laps in three.js
on a greybox loop and one biome backdrop, so the HUD is judged over moving dust, debris and sky. Stills appear only in captures;
never generated cars. The HUD is built the game's way (DEFAULT: DOM/CSS overlays positioned over each tile's viewport, one layer
for all tiles), so its cost is known before C/R tasks commit to it. Every state opens from a **URL fragment** (for the owner and
for the capture script). No CDN (R70).

§3a starting proposals (DEFAULT; the POC designs and shows each as ONE worked proposal with a one-line why; owner
2026-10-03: "don't give me choices on things that are obvious"; alternatives stay in evidence folders, not the gallery):
- Lobby: the warm-up drive behind the QR and player strip (plan §9).
- Grids with a gap: balanced rows first; the last row is centred and its tiles grow wider within the aspect band, so gameplay
  area comes first (master §6.2); any cell still left over shows the join QR and live standings, never black.
- Cameras: third person by default, first person per seat from the controller (master §6.3); mocks show a mixed grid.
- In-world look: master §12.1's comic treatment (faceted cars, 2–3 tone toon ramp, ink outlines, halftone in shadows); if its
  cost at 24 tiles is too high, present the cheapest version that keeps the look (e.g. outlines on cars and debris only) and say why.
- Controller in a dark room: ink/navy base with cream panels and the player's colour; the TV keeps H4's cream panels.
- Lobby at 32 and beyond: compact roster cards (number badge, colour, name, Ready) that reflow into more columns down to the
  guide's legible minimum, then compact to number + name chips. Never a "max players".

## Interfaces
- Consumes: `art/ui/tokens.json`, fonts and components from P1-U01; Spike J's model script (evidence folder, imported by the mock only).
- Provides: the grid pseudocode → P1-R04; HUD layout/cost → P1-R07; lobby/results layouts → P1-R07; host controls → P1-R07/C05;
  caption placement → P1-A03; the TV base the motion reel and world look (P1-U05) render on; captures for the gallery (P1-U04).

## Reuses / gap
Reuses Spike J's model and its 24×24 bench (`spikes/art-pipeline/J-cruze-lowpoly/REPORT.md`). Gap: no TV HUD, reflow, gap, FP/TP-mix, 32-lobby or host-controls reference existed (plan T65).

## Required tests
- A capture script (Playwright, headed on the Mac for the judged set) that opens every state by URL fragment at 1080p and 4K.
- A measurement of HUD text cap height in px at the smallest tile vs the guide's minimum.
- HUD-layer frame cost at 24 and 32 live tiles, headed on the Mac's GPU (never headless/SwiftShader; label browser + backend).
- Fresh-eyes review note against U01's guide.

## Acceptance
In the bead's acceptance field (`br show`); each item is tagged with how it closes.

## Evidence
The capture set + HUD cost table + review note. Commit it under `docs/evidence/P1-U02/`.

## How this bead closes
- `ev:ci`: green Gitea CI on a commit containing this bead, cited as `receipt:<run url>` with a `batch_verify` gate pass (before CI exists, a committed local receipt; while CI is down, the verifier's `batch-verify.sh` receipt).
- `ev:hardware`: a perf/network receipt naming hardware, browser/backend, build and cohort, closed through the evidence close (`batch-verify.sh close <id> --evidence <file>`, P1-F02).

## Working rules
Follow `AGENTS.md` (owner rules first) and `docs/process/bead-workflow.md`: check your own area, commit with `P1-U02` and the bead ID in the message, push, and close this bead once CI is green on a commit containing it (gate pass, ticked items, `receipt:<run url>`).

## Anti-narrowing clause
> Done only when the FELT, observable outcome above holds in the RUNNING game via the real host path. Passing unit/geometry tests is necessary but NOT sufficient.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] [ev:ci] The mocks run offline from a static folder with no network requests outside the folder (no CDN).
- [x] [ev:ci] Every state listed in the contract opens from a URL fragment; the capture script captures each at 1080p and 4K.
- [x] [ev:ci] The grid player animates 1 → 32 → 1 keeping seat order, shows the gap cases N = 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 13 the §3a way (no black cells), and the layout pseudocode is written next to it.
- [x] [ev:ci] HUD text at the smallest tile (32 tiles at 1080p) meets the guide's minimum cap height in px (measured).
- [x] [ev:hardware] HUD layer frame cost at 24 and 32 live tiles, headed on the Mac's GPU, recorded with hardware/browser/backend (`on:mac`, honest labels §13.1).
- [x] [ev:ci] Lobby (2/8/16/32 + larger-N rule), results/intermission (8 and 32), host controls, caption placement, over-3D overlays and the derby Overview reference all exist as states.
- [x] [ev:ci] A fresh-eyes review note compares the captures with U01's guide.

Let the owner judge thumb reach and legibility on a phone (only possible on a phone) before P1-C02/C03/C06/C07 build the
controller: M2's controls as the in-race controller (owner: "the controls are good"), plus lobby/READY, join (M1), settings
(M2), a tutorial prompt and every §11 controller state, in device frames at true CSS sizes and as a **live mock** on the owner's
own phone.

## Scope (owned paths)
`art/ui/poc/phone/` (static HTML/CSS/JS from `tokens.json`; no Three.js).

The real controller app (P1-C02), join flow (C03), scanner (C04), tutorial (C06) and settings (C07). Nothing here sends network traffic.

## Contract and design decisions
- **In-race controller** (M2 in `docs/plans/ux-study-2026-09-29/`): DRIVE stick left, ACTION stick right (R60), with the boost meter,
  wheelie preload and utility ready/cooldown indicators next to the sticks; secondary buttons away from thumbs: Identify,
  camera (chase/first person), Recover, Help, Settings, Leave; the HUD strip. Identify is also the first entry in the controller menu, and
  its full-screen flash (the number, big, in the player's colour) is one of the mocked states.
- Also: lobby with READY, join (M1: code entry + Scan QR code side by side), settings (M2), a tutorial prompt, and **every §11
  controller state**: Finding the game, No such game, Game ended, Preview expired, Connecting, Finding a relay, No route, Ready
  to join, Joining, Playing ("You're #12"), Reconnecting ("Reconnecting as #12…"), Host gone, Host paused, Another tab, Update needed.
- **Portrait and landscape**, in device frames at true CSS sizes: small iPhone 375×667, large iPhone 430×932, mid Android 412×915
  (DEFAULT set).
- **Live mock** on the owner's phone (served over HTTPS from the POC gallery): sticks follow the thumbs and drive the indicators,
  the §11 edge-safe zones are visible (stick zones start ≥ 24 px from screen edges because iOS Safari's edge swipe navigates
  back), a thumb-reach overlay toggles, and nothing is sent anywhere.
- Each stick's states: idle, touched, wheelie preload, utility cooldown, disabled, on autopilot; press/release feedback.
- Uses the **dark-room base** (§3a: ink/navy base, cream panels, the player's colour).
- Touch hygiene matches §11 so the mock behaves like the real thing: `touch-action: none`, no pinch/double-tap zoom, no selection.

- Consumes: tokens/fonts/components from P1-U01.
- Provides: accepted phone layouts → P1-C02 (sticks/HUD), C03 (states/wording), C06 (prompt), C07 (settings); captures → P1-U04.

description:
**Source:** `docs/plans/v0.2-playtest-1-plan.md` §15 **P1-U05** (cites §3a items 9, 10, 13); master cut new (owner 2026-10-03); master §12.1, §12.1a, §6.3 (`docs/plans/v0.2-revamp-plan-2026-09-28.md`).

**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-U01, P1-U02, P1-F11. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
H4 is a painting and the game renders a faceted low-poly car, so the chrome and the world have to be shown together. Render
the in-world look live with the real Cruz Missile under U02's HUD, measure its frame cost at 24 tiles, draw the in-world graphics
in that look, and build a live motion reel with reduced-motion variants. The accepted look is what P1-R10 puts into the engine.

## Scope (owned paths)
`art/ui/poc/world/`, `art/ui/poc/motion/`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Implementing the look in the game renderer (P1-R10); the grid/HUD layouts themselves (P1-U02).

## Contract and design decisions
**(1) The in-world look.** Live in three.js, the real Cruz Missile (Spike J's model) on the greybox and one biome backdrop, under
U02's HUD, at TV size, in a 24-tile grid and in U02's Overview bowl, in the §3a look (master §12.1): faceted with a **2–3 tone toon
ramp**, **ink outlines** (screen-space edge detection on depth + normals + object ID, run once in post) and **halftone in the
shadows**, with a touch of §12.1a's sun-bleached grit. Comic effects never cover identity (number/colour) or the road ahead.
Build it with the vendored shader skills and the `jammers-look` adapter (P1-F11). Measure its frame cost at 24 tiles on the Mac (an outline pass per tile viewport is the likely expense). If too high, find the
cheapest version that keeps the look (e.g. outlines on cars and debris only) and present that, with why.

**(2) In-world graphics** in that look: checkpoint gate and finish-line markers, route edges and barrier colours, wayfinding
chevrons, and how each identity colour reads as **lit paint on the car next to its flat badge**.

**(3) Motion reel**, built live on U02's mocks so timings are real (not a video edit): the countdown, a join (tile appears, grid
reflows), the Identify pulse (master §5.2: ~1.5 s pulse/scale, "#7 THAT'S YOU!" burst, outline in other tiles), a wreck and
respawn (respawn cuts, never swoops), the phase changes (lobby → countdown → race → results) and the results reveal. Each has a
**reduced-motion version** (removes excess shake/flashes without reducing information); durations come from U01's tokens.

§3a starting proposals (DEFAULT; the POC designs and shows each as ONE worked proposal with a one-line why; owner
2026-10-03: "don't give me choices on things that are obvious"; alternatives stay in evidence folders, not the gallery):
- Lobby: the warm-up drive behind the QR and player strip (plan §9).
- Grids with a gap: balanced rows first; the last row is centred and its tiles grow wider within the aspect band, so gameplay
  area comes first (master §6.2); any cell still left over shows the join QR and live standings, never black.
- Cameras: third person by default, first person per seat from the controller (master §6.3); mocks show a mixed grid.
- In-world look: master §12.1's comic treatment (faceted cars, 2–3 tone toon ramp, ink outlines, halftone in shadows); if its
  cost at 24 tiles is too high, present the cheapest version that keeps the look (e.g. outlines on cars and debris only) and say why.

description:

**Depends on (plan IDs):** P1-S08, P1-S04, P1-S05, P1-N06. These are required inputs, not just related work.

## Purpose and observable outcome
The shared item system the boomerang and the sanga plug into: versioned item cards, a two-slot queue per car used in order, and use on the ACTION stick.

## Scope (owned paths)
`crates/jj-sim/src/items/`, `assets/items/*.json` (cards), card validator in `jj-contracts`.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
The two items (W02, W03); pickup stations and boxes (W04); HUD and journeys (W05).

## Contract and design decisions
Owner direction 2026-10-03: before the full test after Playtest 1, the game has **one weapon and one boost-type item**: the
**boomerang** and the **"sanga"** (a sausage on bread). Each player stores **two items, used in the order they were picked up**. Other item
ideas wait (master §9.5's list). Pickups look like **delivery boxes** with the item printed on the outside (R94).
Rules carried from master §9.2: one shared ACTION vertical gesture uses the front item; self-use items work in either vertical direction;
respawn clears held items (no free pickup); spawn-protected cars can't collect or use offensive items; a failed use keeps the item and says
why; fired items keep their causal owner through the owner's respawn and expire naturally or at round end; round-end cleanup removes effects
in the retired world, never live debris; every item lists its counterplay; effects are forces, zones or bounded changes, never scripted poses;
damage goes through the part model (S04).

- **Cards as data** (`assets/items/<id>.json`, validated): id, version, class (projectile/buff), activation (sector entry), direction
  (forward/rear/self), uses, arming, lifetime/duration, cleanup policy, counterplay list (a card without counterplay is rejected), presentation
  hooks, rationale.
- **Two-slot queue per car:** pickups fill the back; ACTION up or down uses the front item and the queue shifts (owner 2026-10-03). A full
  queue doesn't consume a pickup.
- With an empty queue, ACTION up/down keep P1-S08's OI! flash and cone (DEFAULT, harmless fallback); the wire stays the same
  (`utilityForward`/`utilityRear` mean "use forward/rear").
- Damage from items goes through S04's parts; in derby it's credited to the item's owner (S10 attribution).

## Interfaces
- Consumes: S08 actions, S04 damage, S05 respawn/race state, N06. Provides: the item framework to W02–W05, inventory in snapshots/HUD facts.

## Required tests
- Scenarios: queue order, full-queue pass-through, respawn clears, protected car can't use offensive items, failed use keeps the item, round-end cleanup, replay determinism; card validator rejects missing fields or counterplay.

description:

## Purpose and observable outcome
The first boost-type item (owner 2026-10-03): eat a sanga and for a while you shrug off weapons and other cars: you can tank them and just
drive without worrying about their collisions.

## Scope (owned paths)

The framework (W01), pickups (W04).

## Contract and design decisions
Card defaults (TUNE):
- Self-use in either vertical direction; lasts **6 s**; using another sanga while one is active refreshes the timer (no stacking multiplier).
- **Tank:** the car's rigid body gets a higher Rapier dominance group than other cars and debris for the duration, so contacts push them and
  not it (DEFAULT approach; verify the rapier3d 0.36 API and record it). Terrain and barriers still collide normally.
- **Shrug off:** contact damage to it is ignored for the duration; weapon effects on it are ×0.2 (the boomerang's impulse and damage).
- Its own driving is unchanged (no speed boost); it still deals damage when it rams (credited normally in derby).
- Ends at a tick boundary; if it overlaps another car at the end, the separation adds no launch (energy accounting).
- Looks: a warm emissive aura and a sizzle of steam (R12 system), a timer on the controller and the tile.
- Counterplay: it's timed and visible; terrain, barriers and the bowl still matter.

## Required tests
- Scenarios: tank-push (pushes a stationary car aside keeping ≥ 90 % of its speed), ram-immunity (rammed at 15 m/s: no damage and a small heading change), vs-boomerang (×0.2), ends-cleanly (no launch on expiry overlap, energy check), refresh-not-stack.

Put items in the world: delivery-box pickups at replenishing stations on the race tracks and in the derby bowl, drawn fairly.

## Out of scope (owned by neighbouring beads)
Item behaviour (W02, W03).

## Contract and design decisions
- **Look (R94):** every pickup is the same cardboard delivery box with the contained item's image printed on its sides. Generate reference
  sheets for the boomerang, the sanga and the box through the art pipeline first, then code-build the box with a code-drawn print per item.
- **Stations:** map-defined, replenishing; procgen places them along race tracks (on the drivable line's edges, never blocking a jump or the
  start corridor) and around the derby bowl; the greybox gets authored ones. Recharge 5 s game time, visibly.
- **Draws:** deterministic, seeded, from the pool {boomerang, sanga}, independent of race position (no rubber-banding). A full queue doesn't
